Broker schedule. Both the under-0.5% broker gate and 2% first-year gate pass. These are entry/holding charges, not an assumed sale within the year or a dividend-tax estimate. A limit controls the purchase price; the bid/ask spread is not separately measured. Recalculate GBP costs if FX changes.

Two shares would cost £151.71 before fees and exceed the reduced allocation; commission is zero, so buying more would not improve percentage fee drag. Exposure is 15.17% of £500 contributed, with no cap breach. Starting cash is £447.24; this order alone leaves £371.27, or £283.46 if the companion five-share MWA top-up also fills at its limit. Sources: prices, positions, arithmetic at the stated limits.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb monetises institutions moving trading and execution onto electronic networks, with distribution and transaction activity supporting a business beyond the sale of software seats. Revenue grew 18.9% in FY2025 and 9.0% in Q2 2026, while filed operating margins improved, so the case rests on profitable execution activity rather than a Canton Coin revaluation. My inference is that the market is discounting a lasting slowdown in monetisation, whereas continuing client activity offers an opportunity to grow transaction earnings; the durability of that opportunity against a stronger competitor remains the test below. Annual report, Q2 release.

3. Falsifier

Warning: Re-read at the first monthly report after entry if fully electronic US high-grade TRACE share falls below 18.0%, versus 19.0% in August, or at Q3 results if credit revenue declines year on year despite positive credit cash ADV growth. The first tests lost execution activity; the second tests monetisation that total notional volume can conceal. September's monthly release is expected in early October from the observed monthly cadence; check by 9 October 2026, then on 29 October. Thresholds are my decision rules, not management guidance. August baseline, confirmed Q3 date.

Break: Exit under §5.1 if the same fully electronic high-grade share is below 17.0% in three consecutive post-entry monthly observations, or credit revenue falls year on year in both Q3 and Q4 2026 while credit cash ADV grows in both quarters. The share test can break by the November activity report, checked by 10 December 2026; assess the revenue test by 28 February 2027, a review deadline rather than an announced Q4 date. These are independent break paths: strong group earnings do not excuse losing share or giving away credit execution.

Cross-check the competitive explanation against MarketAxess's quarterly credit fee per million and portfolio-trading ADV: Q2 baselines were $129 and $2.0bn, respectively. Its next quarterly release is expected in the autumn, checked by 15 November. The competitor's own disclosure is the external source; its adoption alone does not trigger a sale. Definitions and mix matter, and share denominators must remain comparable. If releases disappear or TRACE methodology changes, record unavailable evidence and re-review rather than treating missing observations as a pass. MarketAxess Q2.

4. Review date

9 October 2026, regardless of price, then 30 October 2026 after confirmed Q3 results. Rule 4's timing does not independently require a smaller order: the share observable is monthly. §7.2a already halves the allocation.

Local check: material disagreement disclosed. Annual local operating income includes the tax-receivable-agreement adjustment: FY2025 is $845.124m locally against filed $835.338m; FY2024 $685.758m against $678.028m; FY2023 $495.752m against $505.269m. The margin series above uses the filing. Q2 revenue, operating income and attributed net income agree. Company-adjusted EPS uses a different share basis and adds back items including acquisition amortisation; it is a cross-check, not certified recurring GAAP EPS or a replacement percentile. The two missing capital ratios stay blank: margin is not ROIC.

Adjustments: The FY2025 release identifies $270.9m gross Canton Coin gains, including $205.4m in Q4. They are not directly subtractable from local shareholder-attributed net income without tax and non-controlling-interest allocation. No safe net adjustment was derived, and zero TW fiscal years carry cited adjustments in the store. The brief's final output-only rule also restricts this run to pot/proposals/; this finding is retained here. The 27.04× cross-check removes other items too and does not certify 261 historical bars. Half-size is the explicit cost of this uncertainty.

6. The case against

Theses: T1, cheaper inference may lower Tradeweb's automation costs and competitors' costs; T2, execution earns transaction fees, but its research and workflow interfaces face the same pressure as other software. Neither thesis proves its transaction fees are protected.

Dominant risk (competitive): Competing execution networks win institutional activity or force lower monetisation, undermining the returns from Tradeweb's network investment.

Earliest observable: Monthly fully electronic high-grade TRACE share, next expected early October; quarterly credit revenue against credit cash ADV on 29 October. MarketAxess's own quarterly fee and adoption data supplies the external comparison. Sources and exact thresholds in P3.

ICE's proposed acquisition of MarketAxess makes the distribution threat concrete; it is a proposed transaction, not a completed combination. ICE announcement. An attractive margin invites competitors. Higher notional volumes may arrive in cheaper protocols, and crypto gains can conceal that erosion. T1/T2 could help every rival simultaneously; the reason to buy is continued monetised execution, not an assertion that AI cannot displace its interface. The historical discount is large, but the unverified earnings distribution cannot demonstrate that the discount is wrong.

Combined exposure: TW is absent from the human holdings, verified against holdings. This adds a new company, but also adds to an already 66.63% US human book (Scan); geography is not independence from its existing financial-market exposures. The £75.85 ticket is about 0.06% of the human book's £127,868 value.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: The case uses filed operating earnings, records the non-operating gains, sizes down for their uncertainty, and tests share and monetisation rather than buying a general electronic-trading growth story. The bet can still lose; its failure need not wait for the share price to explain it.

What decided the shortlist

TW gets the fresh-name allocation. It sells execution, with growing filed operating profits, and the cash equity is available at T212. Its P/E needs qualification: Canton Coin gains and the tax-receivable-agreement classification make local headline profitability look better than the operating business. The proposal halves the allocation and tests monthly execution share and quarterly monetisation. MarketAxess's own Q2 release shows portfolio-trading ADV growth, and ICE's announced acquisition offers a concrete competitive mechanism. Neither is proof that TW loses; that is what the falsifier observes. TW detail and sources.

MWA gets a modest top-up after TW. Its corrected filed margins still improve over several years, while falling asset turnover makes a standalone cash-return test necessary. The new proposal adds independent cash-conversion and margin break paths. It does not silently change the falsifier on the three shares already bought. This is a deliberate preference for its repair business over the unresolved cases below, not allocation by habit. MWA detail and sources.

NFLX is the closest unfunded fresh candidate. Local Q2 revenue $12.559938bn and operating profit $4.192610bn agree with the July shareholder letter. H1 view hours grew only2%, while price changes help revenue; management is also reducing aggregate viewing disclosure to annual publication. The relevant uncertainty is whether higher monetisation remains compatible with engagement, not whether streaming exists. Nielsen's May US observation showed Netflix8.0% of TV usage versus YouTube13.8%; it does not demonstrate a Netflix share collapse, and it is neither current-week nor global evidence. I prefer to await Q3 operating evidence and the next available same-market Nielsen observations, reviewed 21 October after the locally estimated20 October results. T1 bears on cheaper production and competing content; T2 is not a direct seat-pricing exposure. This is a business-conviction wait, not a rule that incomplete normalisation forbids an order: §7.2a could permit a half-size position, but it cannot supply conviction about engagement.

INTU: wait for the17 September Investor Day, review18 September. The FY2026 release reports US TurboTax units39.0m versus39.9m, down2%, while TurboTax revenue rose7%. T2 may already be arriving through fewer units offset by price/mix; T1 can lower its input costs without protecting those units. The local annual series still ends July2025, so it cannot independently confirm the full FY2026 accounts. I want customer/usage evidence from the announced Investor Day, not another revenue-growth assertion. The very large de-rating alone does not disprove the market's worry, and one-share affordability is not the reason for waiting.

RELX: exclude this cycle under the business-thesis requirement. Reported19.95× against local median34.1008× is a 41.49% de-rating. T2 directly bears on legal/research workflow value and T1 can lower competitors' inference costs. The H1 release reports stronger underlying growth, useful counterevidence to immediate collapse. But Harvey's dated9 September statement says80% of the Am Law100 use it: a competitor's own adoption claim, not verified displacement of Lexis seats. Adoption disclosures are irregular, not quarterly. I cannot yet argue convincingly that RELX's discount overstates this risk; saying its content is trusted would merely assert the rebuttal. This is not a permanent T2 exclusion or a refusal for uncertified EPS.

RSGN: wait until the16 September final interim report, review17 September. The immediate CEO departure creates a real execution question just before the scheduled report. The local144-week window is short and indicative, starting after the SPAC period. Strong historical capital ratios cannot establish whether the incoming leadership can deliver the current expansion. No venue-cost veto is being applied: any future order must separately establish broker availability and Swiss charges.

LULU: exclude on the business, and flag a wrong stored adjustment. Its 3 September release guides Q3 revenue down10–11%, with Q2 operating margin18.8% including a5.6-point tariff-refund benefit. That is evidence of deteriorating trading, not a clean rebound thesis. The existing adjustment also attributes a Q2 period ending 2 August2026 benefit to the fiscal year ending 31 January2026. It subtracts $134.5m pre-tax refunds from net income and labels that amount as including interest, although the release separately states $4.1m interest and $0.86/share after-tax total benefit. The stored own percentile is therefore not certified. This error is documented, not silently repaired or used as the sole reason to reject the business.

MWA — Mueller Water Products

What it does: Mueller makes valves, hydrants, meters and other equipment used to distribute and measure water. Municipal water systems and construction customers buy its products for new installations and repairs. Company filing.

Research dated 10 September 2026. Run report and complete ranking. This is a proposed top-up; it does not rewrite the conditions Leo accepted for the existing three shares.

1. Order

BUY 5 additional shares of MWA on NYSE, limit $23.69 per share, regular session only. Use Trading 212 Invest or Stocks ISA; cash-equity availability and the original holding's T212 execution in holdings support the venue. Day order for 11 September 2026; expire if unfilled.

Currency USD. At local GBP/USD 1.3509, the ticket is $118.45 = £87.68. The £250 maximum position less the existing £52.61 marked holding gives £197.39 normal headroom; §7.2a halves that to an allocation of £98.70. Five whole shares use 88.84% of it, leaving £11.01 before fees, £10.88 after fees, using unrounded arithmetic. This conservative sizing recognises unquantified tariff refunds, the one-time tax benefit and the historical operating-income discrepancy.

Broker schedule. Both cost gates pass. Costs assume a one-year hold, not a sale or a particular dividend-tax status; the live spread is unmeasured and the limit caps price. Six shares would cost £105.22, exceeding the reduced allocation without improving percentage fees. No one-share or fee-driven cap exception is used.

The resulting 8 shares are £140.29, or 28.06% of £500 contributed. This top-up alone leaves £359.43 of the recorded £447.24 cash. If both this and TW fill at their limits, cash remaining is £283.46, including both entry fees. Prices, positions.

Why a top-up: The fresh TW proposal is funded first. MWA's repair/replacement business and multi-year filed profit improvement warrant a modest additional position, whereas NFLX needs a stronger engagement/monetisation case, INTU needs customer-unit evidence, and RSGN faces an immediate management transition before its final interim report. None is rejected for a prior draft or for overlap with the human book. MWA stays far below the 50% limit, and its capital/cash test is strengthened for these new shares in response to the latest Review.

2. Thesis

Mueller supplies equipment required to maintain water systems, giving it a demand source beyond new housing construction. Filed operating profit improved across FY2023–25, and the foundry investment offers a specific opportunity to turn that larger profit base into cash after capital expenditure. My inference is that the market may be treating current volume softness as lasting while underweighting repair demand, but the investment earns its place only if expanded capacity delivers cash returns without repeated exceptional income. Annual accounts, June filing, operating outlook.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At FY2026 results, trigger a full re-read if consolidated physical volumes decline again, or full-year free cash flow is 70% or less of company-reconciled adjusted net income. Check by 10 November 2026, against the local 5 November estimate, not a confirmed release. Use the sales bridge's stated volume direction if units are unavailable; silence is missing evidence. The cash threshold comes from management's commitment to exceed 70%. Q3 release.

Break: By the Q2 FY2027 release, checked no later than 15 May 2027, exit these proposed shares under §5.1 if trailing-twelve-month (operating cash flow − capital expenditure) / reconciled adjusted net income is 60% or less, independent of volumes or margin. Also break earlier if two successive post-entry quarters have filed GAAP operating margins below 18%, independent of volume direction. A non-positive earnings denominator is not a passing ratio: if TTM GAAP operating profit is non-positive, the earnings thesis itself breaks. These are my thresholds, not company guidance; the May date is a review deadline, not an announced release.

For the cash test, derive March-2027 TTM values as FY2026 minus H1 FY2026 plus H1 FY2027, using the same company reconciliation each time. Keep recurring factory spending in capital expenditure; do not add it back to manufacture cash conversion. Separately show the denominator after any quantified one-time income and document definition changes. A missing reconciliation or unannounced result triggers review and remains unassessed, never a pass. The warning arrives at FY results before the TTM break; the independent margin path prevents stable volumes from hiding deteriorating profitability.

This addresses the Review's criticism that the accepted proposal's break required both declining volumes and low margins. It does not retrospectively trigger a sale of the original three shares.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, then 28 February 2027 and 15 May 2027 for the independent break tests. The dominant risk has observable cash/volume evidence within the next quarter, so Rule 4 does not add a second reduction to the §7.2a half-size.

5. Numbers as of today

Snapshot 20:35:57 UTC, 10 September 2026; MWA regular price struck 20:00:03 UTC. Sources for local figures are prices, earnings and positions.

Local check: disagreement disclosed and filed numbers used. The local annual margins are 10.79%, 16.26% and 18.84%, and Q3 operating income is $91.8m. These exceed filed GAAP values because charges are missing from that operating-income field. The corrected series still improves, but the higher local series is not evidence for the thesis. Reported EPS and vendor norm remain labelled local measures, not a certified clean earnings base.

Adjustments: The release quantifies a $0.06/share Q3 FY2026 one-time tax benefit; the June filing also names tariff refunds but does not separately quantify them. The matching annual FY2026 row is not yet in earnings.json, so attaching this benefit to the latest FY2025 row would be wrong. Zero MWA fiscal years carry stored cited adjustments. No entry was appended: the brief's final rule restricts writes to pot/proposals/, and the future fiscal-year mapping is not yet available. The sensitivity above removes only the known tax benefit; the allocation is halved because it is incomplete.

6. The case against

Theses: none.

Dominant risk (financial): Expanded factory capital fails to earn cash returns, while pricing and temporary benefits make reported margins look stronger than underlying demand.

Earliest observable: Full-year operating cash flow less capex relative to adjusted net income, and the consolidated volume bridge, at FY2026 results expected in November. These are company quarterly/annual disclosures; P3 uses cash conversion independently of volume and margin.

The falling local turnover series makes this risk visible already. Repair demand is not an unlimited municipal budget, and the company identifies weak residential construction, inflation and further legacy-foundry costs. High margins could partly reflect temporary pricing protection and refunds. June filing. A tax adjustment alone cannot validate the percentile; the smaller order accepts that uncertainty without describing it as solved.

Combined exposure: Holdings shows only the three pot-tagged MWA shares, with no separate human MWA holding. The proposed addition is about 0.069% of the £127,868 human-book value, and still adds US exposure to a human book already 66.63% US (Scan). Pot concentration rises from 10.52% to 28.06% of contributions; the fresh TW order does not make that concentration disappear.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: The argument does not extrapolate a general infrastructure rebound. It checks a corrected filed profit series, explicitly confronts weaker capital turnover, and requires cash after factory spending. A stable sales story with inadequate cash returns can now break the new thesis on its own.

TW — Tradeweb Markets

What it does: Tradeweb runs electronic marketplaces where banks, asset managers and other institutions trade bonds, interest-rate products and other securities. It earns transaction fees, subscriptions and data revenue. Its ordinary business is arranging trades, rather than taking the investment risk in those trades itself. Company description and revenue categories.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of TW on Nasdaq through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA, limit $102.94, regular session only. Currency USD. Day order for 10 September 2026; an unfilled order expires and is not chased.

Allocate £125, half the normal £250 maximum under §7.2a because the earnings distribution is materially uncertified. Deploy £75.94, leaving £49.06 of that allocation before fees. Rates are USD per currency unit: $102.94 / 1.3555 = £75.9425. Expected entry FX is £0.11 (0.15%), commission £0, custody £0, ADR fees £0, purchase transaction tax £0. Expected first-year broker/holding costs, assuming no sale, are therefore approximately 0.15%, below both §4.1a and §4.1. Dividends are not forecast or treated as fee-free investment returns; personal dividend tax is outside this dealing-cost calculation. Instrument availability, broker fees, dividend FX treatment.

The position is 15.19% of £500 contributed, so neither the one-share nor fee exception is needed. Two shares would cost £151.88 before fees and exceed the half allocation; adding a share produces no percentage fee saving. The risk in P6 has monthly and quarterly observables, so Rule 4 adds no separate reduction. These are estimates at the stored FX rate, not a promise about the execution conversion.

Actual starting cash is £447.38. This order alone leaves £371.32 after estimated FX. Together with this run's four-share MWA proposal, total new deployment is £146.74, estimated FX £0.22, and cash left idle £300.42. Neither draft reserves money or records a trade. The 77-name screen explains why the remaining cash stays idle. Sources: positions, prices.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb can earn more from institutional trading moving onto electronic venues without needing to lend the principal traded, and its latest reported quarter shows revenue and operating profit growing together. The business opportunity is greater use of its transaction network, with existing infrastructure serving additional flow; August's fully electronic US credit volumes support that adoption case, while lower revenue per unit makes its durability a live test. My inference is that the discount overstates the risk that automation destroys aggregate trading economics: unlike a disappearing software seat, an executed transaction still generates a fee, but P3 must establish whether adoption actually outweighs fee compression. Quarterly results, August activity.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: the case rests on filed operating profit, fee-paying activity and observable market share, not a macro trading-volume rebound or a low P/E alone. A high margin is not proof of a moat. I infer that connecting both sides of institutional trades and embedding execution into their workflows can preserve some economics; the fee and share tests below explicitly allow that inference to fail. The reported multiple is about 55.72% below its local historical median, but gains in investments contaminate that comparison. I do not describe the whole difference as an unjustified market discount or promise a return to the median.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At the September activity report, check by 9 October 2026, re-read if fully electronic US high-grade share is below 18.0% or high-yield share below 7.5%, against August's 19.0% and 8.3%. At Q3 results, locally dated 29 October, also warn if cash-credit fee per million falls more than 15% year on year, or credit revenue stops growing despite rising credit volume. These are my decision thresholds, not management guidance. They test customer loss and weakening monetisation before total company earnings necessarily fall. August baseline, quarterly fee disclosure.

Break: Recommend exit under §5.1 if, in each of Q3 and Q4 2026, cash-credit fee per million falls more than 15% year on year and credit revenue declines, even if trading volume or group profit rises. Independently, break if high-grade share is below 17.0%, or high-yield below 7.0%, in three consecutive post-entry monthly disclosures. Review these by 28 February 2027, using earlier observations as they arrive. A lost customer franchise or persistently worse revenue economics can therefore fail the thesis without a group margin collapse. Missing or redefined disclosure is a review trigger, never an assumed pass.

External check: MarketAxess's Q2 release shows credit fee per million falling from $138 to $129 and portfolio-trading ADV rising 33%. This is evidence that automation can grow activity while weakening unit economics across the industry. Compare like-for-like product fee trends at subsequent quarterly disclosures, and use FINRA TRACE monthly volume reports for the market denominator; publication is the third business day after month-end. MarketAxess has suspended monthly press releases following its announced ICE transaction, so do not invent a monthly rival-release cadence. Its volume-page access failed here, and the FINRA index returned an older vintage: neither supplies a verified current rival share. Those gaps limit attribution, but the dated Tradeweb fee/revenue and share tests remain usable.

4. Review date

9 October 2026, regardless of price. Financial follow-up 30 October 2026; the 29 October results date comes from the local calendar, not a newly verified issuer announcement. Final two-quarter test by 28 February 2027.

5. Numbers as of today

Local prices fetched 2026-09-10 05:45:29 UTC; the regular TW price was struck 2026-09-09 20:00 UTC. The Scan uses the same fetch. No extended-hours price enters sizing.

Local check: disagreements disclosed. FY2025 local operating income is $845.124m, versus $835.338m filed: the difference is the $9.786m tax-receivable-agreement adjustment. FY2024 local $685.758m similarly includes $7.730m above filed operating income. I use the filed subtotals for margins. The local FY2025 ni of $812.792m is parent-attributable income; the release's $921.500m headline includes non-controlling interests. These are different bases, not missing profit. Local EPS $4.19 is consistent within rounding with the $4.18 sum of its quarterly EPS.

Adjustments: Zero TW fiscal years have entries in adjustments. The FY2025 release identifies $205.4m Q4 Canton Coin gains, a pre-tax consolidated amount. It does not separately give their after-tax amount attributable to the parent; subtracting $205.4m directly from local parent net income would invent an adjustment. The company-adjusted $3.79 TTM is an explicitly different, broader basis, including amortisation and assumed tax/share adjustments, not my certified recurring EPS. No exact net-income entry was writable from that disclosure. This material uncertainty is why P1 halves the allocation; the 5.914th percentile is a screening indication, not proof that the adjusted TTM lies in its own historical decile.

6. The case against

Theses: T2 bears on automated execution and the subscription/data portions of the business: cheaper workflow can compress fees even as trades rise. T1 is an indirect input-cost mechanism for that automation, not evidence of improved shareholder returns.

Dominant risk (competitive): Rival venues and automated execution drive fee compression faster than additional paid activity can compensate.

Earliest observable: September market shares in the next monthly activity report, checked by 9 October; product fee per million and credit revenue at the Q3 release. The external comparator and its changed cadence are specified in P3.

Credit economics could deteriorate while rates or investment gains keep group earnings attractive. The proposed ICE/MarketAxess combination adds a better-resourced competitor; MarketAxess's current fee decline is a warning about the industry, not proof that Tradeweb has won. Capital turnover is only 0.251×, and missing local ROIC means I cannot call the whole invested balance sheet efficient. A cheap reported distribution can be a side effect of gains outside the trading franchise.

Combined exposure: TW is absent from both the human holdings and actual pot holdings. This starts a new company exposure of about £75.94 and adds to an already large US allocation. The Scan reports 66.56% US for its aggregate book, which includes the tagged MWA pot trade; it is not a perfectly separated human-only weight. Holdings, Scan book, pot positions.

model: gpt-6-astra, lane: deepdive, 2026-09-10 05:45, 13m49s, 3,839,255 tokens (186,085 fresh, 3,632,256 cached, 20,914 out), stamped from the session log rather than self-reported

MWA — Mueller Water Products

What it does: Mueller makes valves, hydrants, meters and other equipment used to move and measure water. Utilities, municipalities and construction customers buy those products for water networks. It earns from manufacturing and selling equipment. Company Q3 filing.

1. Order

BUY 4 additional shares of MWA on NYSE through Trading 212 Invest/Stocks ISA, limit $23.99, regular session only. Currency USD. Day order for 10 September 2026, expiring unfilled rather than chasing the price. This takes the actual holding from 3 to 7 shares.

Normal maximum exposure is £250, 50% of £500 contributed. Apply §7.2a to the whole resulting holding, giving a £125 ceiling because the earnings adjustments and operating-income field are uncertain. The existing three shares mark at £53.09, leaving approximately £71.91 of exposure room. Four shares deploy £70.79; seven shares mark at £123.89, or 24.78% of contributions, leaving £1.11 below that half ceiling. Eight shares would cost £141.59, so another share is not justified by idle cash. No cap exception is used. Positions, prices and FX, at $1.3555/£.

Expected costs: £0 commission, £0.11 FX (0.15% of the ticket), £0 custody, £0 ADR fee and £0 purchase transaction tax. First-year broker/holding costs assuming no sale are approximately 0.15%, clearing §4.1a and §4.1. The percentage does not improve with more shares. Ordinary market bid/offer spread and any future sale costs are not represented as a known fixed fee. T212 listing, fee schedule.

Starting cash £447.38 becomes £376.48 after this order alone and estimated FX. If this run's one-share TW order also fills, cash becomes £300.42. The allocations share that one cash balance; neither uses hypothetical additional funding.

Why a top-up under §4.5a: TW is the fresh candidate that clears my business assessment and is funded first. Another TW share exceeds its £125 uncertainty allocation. Among the remaining names, R&S's falling orders and deliveries make capacity payback less convincing today; Netflix's weak growth in viewing hours makes price-led growth less persuasive than it appears; and the software candidates need a stronger response to T2. MWA's filed margin improvement predates its latest tax benefit, and its cash and capital tests can now be specified directly. That supports this modest increase, not a move to the 50% cap. The full screen accounts for alternatives. No unexecuted earlier draft affects the choice.

2. Thesis

Mueller offers a way to own the replacement and measurement equipment inside existing water networks, with an established product business rather than a forecast that water scarcity alone creates profits. Filed annual operating margins improved from 9.99% in FY2023 to 18.23% in FY2025 on rising sales, before the current quarter's one-time tax benefit. My inference is that the market undervalues some of that earlier operating improvement, but the investment only works if the resulting profits become cash and adequately reward the assets required to produce them. Filed annual statements.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: I am not treating infrastructure demand or this quarter's pricing as proof of profitable growth. Local turnover declined while margins rose. Established specifications and the installed equipment base may help defend the economics, but I treat this as a hypothesis; the factory-return and cash tests below can reject it even if headline revenue continues rising.

3. Falsifier

The 10 September Review identifies a gap in the existing thesis: a margin-plus-volume break can miss poor capital returns. These are proposed tests for this top-up; writing them does not retrospectively replace the accepted three-share holding's terms. If Leo accepts the top-up as a revised company thesis, the Review should explicitly record that adoption.

Warning: At FY2026 results, checked by 10 November 2026, re-read upon any of: another disclosed decline in consolidated physical volumes; free cash flow at or below 70% of company-adjusted net income; or filed operating income / year-end total assets below 13.5%. The cash threshold is management's commitment; the return threshold is my decision rule against a 14.17% FY2025 baseline. Volumes come from the sales bridge, not a price-driven revenue percentage. No volume disclosure means unavailable evidence, not flat volume. Q3 outlook, annual operating income, balance sheet.

Break: Recommend exit under §5.1 if FY2026 filed operating income / year-end total assets is below 12%, or FY2026 free cash flow is below 50% of company-adjusted net income. Check by 10 November 2026, or immediately when the annual filing supplies the denominator. Independently, two successive September and December quarters with filed GAAP operating margin below 18% in each break the case, checked by 28 February 2027, whether or not reported volume also falls. These are my thresholds, not forecasts or management guidance.

Define free cash flow as operating cash flow less capital expenditure, and use the company's reconciled adjusted net income for the cash-conversion test. Define operating return on assets as full-year filed GAAP operating income / the same year-end's total assets, retaining goodwill and cash: this deliberately tests all capital tied up, not only selected factory assets. It is pre-tax operating ROA, not ROIC. A disclosed material impairment of the expanded production assets prompts immediate review rather than waiting for the annual ratios. If accounts are delayed, review that delay explicitly; never manufacture a threshold result.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, irrespective of price. The local expected result date is 5 November, estimated, not issuer-confirmed. Follow up by 28 February 2027 for the two-quarter margin test. Existing accepted-thesis reviews continue on their own schedule.

6. The case against

P3 can break independently on weak cash conversion or capital returns, so growing sales and a high margin cannot conceal the risk.

The latest consolidated sales increase was price-led with slightly lower volumes. Tariff refunds and reduced incentive compensation helped profitability, so carrying the quarter's margin forward would be optimistic. Inventory was $379.8m at June, against $328.7m at September, while total assets rose to $1,953.3m; capital is being tied up before its return is settled. Q3 filing. TW — Tradeweb Markets

What it does: Tradeweb operates electronic marketplaces where institutions and dealers trade bonds, derivatives and other financial instruments. It earns transaction fees and sells subscriptions and market data; it does not own the securities customers trade. Company description.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of TW on NASDAQ, limit $103.00, regular session, DAY order for 10 September 2026. Currency USD. Use Trading 212 Invest or Stocks ISA, where TW is listed. Leo executes; this document records no fill.

The normal ceiling is £250, 50% of £500 contributed, not half the £447.43 remaining cash. §7.2a halves the allocation to £125 because neither the vendor nor the historical earnings distribution is certified free of investment gains. One share deploys £76.05, leaving £48.95 of the allocation before costs. Two cost £152.11 and exceed the reduced allocation. No one-share or fee exception is used.

Commission £0, FX 0.15% = £0.1141, custody £0, purchase transaction tax £0, ADR custody £0 because this is ordinary stock. Expected entry and first-year holding charges are £0.1141, 0.15% of the ticket, assuming no sale; both §4.1a and §4.1 pass. Bid/ask spread is market-dependent and the limit bounds the purchase price. A larger order does not reduce the percentage fee. Broker schedule.

Using local USD/GBP 1.3543, cash after TW alone is £371.26. This cycle also proposes 2 NFLX and 4 additional MWA: combined purchases £259.17, FX £0.3888, cash remaining £187.87. TW is 15.21% of contributed capital. These are estimates at the limits; recheck GBP costs at execution and keep each position within its stated reduced ceiling. Do not chase an expired limit.

Fresh names receive allocation before the MWA top-up under §4.5a. Older unexecuted drafts have no allocation or ranking weight.

2. Thesis

Tradeweb turns recurring institutional trading into fee income, with revenues rising from $1.338bn in FY2023 to $2.052bn in FY2025 and filed operating margins improving from 39.28% in FY2024 to 40.70% in FY2025. August's 13.7% year-on-year ADV growth makes the shift toward electronic execution a current business observation rather than merely a forecast. The 55.7% reported multiple discount to its historical median could be T2's automation-driven fee compression being priced; Q2 transaction-fee growth of 8.3% is my evidence for testing whether that discount overstates the damage, not a premise that fees or margins must survive. Local financials, filed annual results, August activity.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At the 29 October 2026 Q3 release, re-read if total variable fees per million fall more than 10% year on year, or cash-credit fees per million fall more than 15%, independently of total revenue growth. Q2 baselines are $2.14 and $114.03, down 7.2% and 11.4%. These are my deterioration thresholds, not management guidance. Also review any two consecutive monthly declines in Tradeweb's fully electronic US high-grade or high-yield share versus the corresponding prior-year months.

Break: By 28 February 2027, exit the proposed share under §5.1 if either fee measure breaches its warning threshold in both Q3 and Q4, even if ADV, market share and total revenue rise. Persistent fee erosion itself invalidates the expected economics; it is not conditional on also losing market share. Missing comparable data triggers review, never an automatic pass. Changes in product mix are investigated at warning and do not silently erase the precommitted break.

Fee definitions and baselines: Q2 10-Q, pp. 54–57. Results date: issuer announcement. February is my assessment deadline, not an announced Q4 date.

4. Review date

9 October 2026, for September activity, irrespective of price. Review again 30 October after Q3, and by 28 February 2027 for the break.

A deliberately harsh sensitivity subtracts the entire pre-tax $205.4m from attributable earnings using that quarter's implied diluted shares: 4.18 - 205.4 / (324.992 / 1.51) = $3.226, giving 31.91×. This over-deducts tax and minority effects, is not a certified recurring EPS, and does not clean 261 historical observations. Reported P/E is 55.7% below its reported median; the sensitivity is 42.5% below that same, unadjusted median. Neither difference is evidence that a discount cannot be justified.

Adjustments: zero TW fiscal years have entries in adjustments.json. No net-income adjustment is writable from the $205.4m gross gain alone: its separate after-tax, attributable amount was not established. Recording gross group income as a deduction from attributable net income would invent a reconciliation. The sensitivity and §7.2a half-size make that limitation explicit; the stored percentile remains the provisional gate, not a claim of certified cheapness.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: execution income, fee capture and filed operating profit carry the argument; a fashionable automation narrative and a low P/E do not. Turnover is modest and ROIC is unavailable. Network economics may protect margins, but competing execution routes and lower-value flow can defeat them; P3 makes that claim testable.

6. The case against

Theses: T2, because automation can shift trading away from paid workflow subscriptions toward execution priced by outcome.

Dominant risk (financial): The flow added by automation earns progressively less per unit, so the network grows without preserving its economics.

Earliest observable: Quarterly fee capture, next on 29 October 2026; monthly electronic share provides an earlier competitive check. P3 can deteriorate while reported revenue is still growing, so Rule 4 does not require another halving.

The T2 discount is plausible: reported P/E is 55.7% below its historical median. My limited counterargument is the still-growing transaction-fee business and current adoption, not that AI cannot displace it. Outside Tradeweb, BGC's PortfolioMatch ADV grew 82% to $431m in Q2; follow that same quarterly series at its next filing, reviewed by 15 November 2026. It demonstrates that competing automation is also being adopted, though its scope is not comparable to all Tradeweb ADV. A further >50% year-on-year increase alongside either TW fee warning accelerates review; rival growth alone is not a sell rule. BGC Q2 filing. Also inspect FINRA's monthly corporate-bond volumes, published on the third business day, before interpreting market-share claims; capped volume is not an interchangeable denominator for uncapped company notional.

Investment gains obscure the earnings base, and historical margin expansion does not establish returns on acquisition capital. These are reasons for the smaller position.

Total exposure: No TW position exists in the human book or pot. The order adds a US-listed financial business to a book whose stored US weight is 66.40%, not to an existing large TW holding. Holdings, Scan book.

NFLX — Netflix

What it does: Netflix buys and produces films, series and other video programming, and distributes them through a subscription service. It earns subscription payments and advertising revenue from its advertising-supported offering. Company letter.

1. Order

BUY 2 shares of NFLX on NASDAQ, limit $76.00, regular session, DAY order for 10 September 2026. Currency USD. Use Trading 212 Invest or Stocks ISA; NFLX is available. The limit is below the $76.03 local close; leave it unfilled rather than chase.

The normal £250 ceiling is halved to £125 under §7.2a: both stored trailing earnings measures include an exceptional payment and the historical percentile is uncertified. The same reduced size also reflects incomplete global engagement disclosure; reductions are not compounded for the same uncertainty. Two shares deploy £112.24, with £12.76 of the reduced allocation unused before fees. A third costs £168.35 and would exceed it. No cap exception is invoked.

At local USD/GBP 1.3543, commission £0, FX 0.15% = £0.1684, custody £0, purchase transaction tax £0, ADR charge £0. Expected first-year holding charges, assuming no sale, are £0.1684 or 0.15%; both cost gates pass. The spread is market-dependent, with the purchase price bounded by the limit. More shares would not reduce percentage charges. Broker schedule.

Cash after this order alone: £335.03. Alongside 1 TW and 4 additional MWA, purchases total £259.17, FX £0.3888, cash left £187.87. NFLX becomes 22.45% of £500 contributed. All GBP amounts are estimates at limits; confirm current FX keeps each position within its reduced ceiling. These are proposals, not executed trades. NFLX is fresh to the pot and receives allocation ahead of the MWA top-up under §4.5a.

2. Thesis

Netflix has spread its content and distribution costs across a growing revenue base: local annual revenue rose from $33.72bn in FY2023 to $45.18bn in FY2025 while operating margin increased from 20.62% to 29.49%. The advertising business adds another source of payment for the same viewing inventory, with management targeting about $3bn in 2026 advertising revenue. My inference is that monetisation and operating leverage can still create value even as subscription growth matures; neither the Warner termination payment nor the assertion that Netflix will beat every substitute belongs in that thesis. Local annual accounts, Q2 shareholder letter.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At each monthly review, trigger a re-read if Netflix's share of US TV viewing in Nielsen's The Gauge is at least 5% lower relative to the same month a year earlier in two consecutive published months, irrespective of revenue or margin. Also warn if Netflix discloses falling total global view hours at its next annual engagement release. These are my thresholds, not company guidance. Revenue growing while audience share falls does not clear the warning.

Break: By 28 February 2027, exit these proposed shares under §5.1 if the comparable Nielsen share is at least 10% lower year on year for three consecutive published months. This is a direct sustained-loss-of-attention test and requires neither a revenue miss nor lower margins. It can fire sooner if the three observations arrive earlier. Monthly seasonality is handled with same-month comparisons, not a June-to-July comparison.

Use Nielsen's monthly source and its underlying releases. The latest retrieved release covers June, published 18 August; it is not September audience data. Nielsen flags methodology changes this autumn: use comparable or restated observations, and escalate an unavailable comparison for review rather than count it as a pass. This US-TV proxy misses phones and international audiences, so it cannot fully falsify global competitive risk.

The separate operating check is the next Q3 result: compare reported operating margin with the 33.2% company forecast. A miss prompts review, but cannot replace the audience test. Company forecast and engagement cadence.

4. Review date

9 October 2026, irrespective of price, for the next accessible Nielsen release. Review again 21 October after the locally estimated 20 October Q3 date, and monthly thereafter through the break deadline. The earnings date is an estimate, not issuer confirmation.

5. Numbers as of today

Local snapshot: prices.json, 9 September 2026, 20:25:59 UTC; regular quote 20:00:00 UTC. earnings.json supplies filed-year and quarterly comparisons, and positions.json supplies £447.43 cash, £500 contributions and no NFLX holding.

Local check: revenue and operating earnings agree; “normalized” net income does not mean clean. Q1 norm = ni = $5.282791bn locally includes the $2.8bn Warner termination payment recorded below operating profit. Four local quarterly EPS sum to $3.177, explaining the quote's rounded $3.18 rather than validating its recurrence. Q1 shareholder letter.

A conservative sensitivity deducts the entire pre-tax receipt, with no assumed tax benefit, using Q1's 4.298bn diluted shares: 3.177 - 2.8 / 4.298 = $2.5255, or 30.10×. This is a stress calculation, not an after-tax recurring EPS. The $2.53 FY2025 base independently gives 30.05×. Reported P/E is 45.1% below its reported historical median; the stress multiple is 30.8% below that same, uncorrected median. None certifies a cheapest-decile position on a consistently adjusted history. §7.2a permits the disclosed provisional gate at half size; I am not relabelling the stored 4.21% percentile as clean.

Adjustments: zero NFLX years have cited adjustments in the store. The receipt belongs to FY2026-12-31, which is not yet a filed annual row in earnings.json; its separately attributable after-tax EPS effect is also unestablished. No entry can safely be attached to FY2025 or subtract a gross payment from filed net income. Preserve the finding here pending the proper annual period and tax reconciliation. FY2025's operating returns predate the receipt.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: the case uses a multi-year operating-margin and capital-return record, prices the business without requiring the windfall, and tests consumption separately from revenue. A cheap reported P/E and enthusiasm for AI or entertainment would not suffice.

6. The case against

Theses: none. Netflix sells consumer entertainment access, not task-priced workflow seats under T2 or frontier-model access under T1. Cheap generated video remains a relevant competitive scenario even though neither standing thesis names it.

Dominant risk (competitive): Other entertainment, including creator and generated video, takes viewing time while price rises and advertising temporarily conceal the loss in revenue.

Earliest observable: Nielsen's monthly US-TV viewing shares, next checked 9 October, with publication lag explicitly retained. Netflix's global view-hours series moves to annual publication in Q1 2027, with no exact date established; the smaller allocation also pays for this slower and incomplete global observable.

Nielsen's June release places YouTube at 13.8% of viewing and shows competing sports and streaming services capturing attention. It also says Netflix viewing increased month on month; neither fact proves lasting displacement or immunity. A US panel will miss an international or mobile-led deterioration.

The company can increase content commitments ahead of cash receipts, and the exceptional payment inflates the impression of cash generation as well as earnings. Strong historical ROIC does not guarantee the next content dollar earns the same return. The warning and break deliberately remain able to fire while P2's revenue and margin figures still look healthy.

Total exposure: The human book holds 20 NFLX shares, approximately 0.88% of its stored market value; this adds two and makes 22 combined, not a new economic exposure. It is not already a large individual holding, but it adds to the 66.40% US book. Holdings, Scan book. Its overlap does not change the ranking.

MWA then earns a smaller top-up because its corrected multi-year operating improvement is stronger evidence than NVO's still-flat-to-falling outlook, PDD's reinvestment-dependent earnings or RSGN's disrupted delivery/leadership transition. The top-up uses the newly increased contribution base, not the mere existence of yesterday's draft. It does not take MWA to the 50% cap or assume a better demand outlook since purchase. The full ranking is in the TW appendix.

2. Thesis

Mueller supplies equipment that existing water systems must maintain and replace, providing a recurring use for its manufacturing capacity. Its filed operating margin rose from 9.99% in FY2023 to 13.82% in FY2024 and 18.23% in FY2025, while annual sales rose from $1.276bn to $1.430bn. My inference is that weak construction expectations may be obscuring a business whose operations have already improved over several years, but the proposed return depends on those assets producing cash rather than on another round of price rises or tax benefits. Filed annual statements, local annual revenue.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At FY2026 results, locally estimated for 5 November 2026, re-read if consolidated physical volumes decline again year on year, or GAAP operating margin is below 19%, or full-year free cash flow does not exceed 70% of adjusted net income. Any one is sufficient. The volume statement may be directional, as in the current filing; an omitted bridge is unavailable evidence, not stable volumes. The cash reference is management's commitment; 19% is my early-warning threshold.

Break: For these additional shares, exit under §5.1 if GAAP operating margin is below 18% in each of two successive post-entry quarters, assessed by 28 February 2027, regardless of sales growth. This standalone margin test addresses the Review's concern that price-led growth could keep a combined margin-and-growth test green. Also break if management discloses a material permanent shutdown or impairment of the capacity on which the efficiency case depends; ordinary restructuring expense alone is not that event.

Use filed operating profit after reorganisation charges. The new margin-only test can fire while price rises keep revenue growing. It does not retrospectively change the conditions Leo accepted on the original three shares in the 8 September proposal; the Review must distinguish the original holding and this proposed top-up until Leo adopts a common rule. Current quarter filing, cash-conversion commitment.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, irrespective of price, or earlier if FY2026 results arrive sooner and trip a warning. Assess the two-quarter break by 28 February 2027; this is a review deadline, not a confirmed Q1 reporting date.

5. Numbers as of today

Local check: an accounting subtotal is wrong, not just a label. The stored annual operating incomes of $137.6m, $213.8m and $269.4m include amounts excluded from the filed operating subtotals of $127.4m, $181.7m and $260.6m for FY2023–25. Q3 similarly carries $91.8m locally versus $80.6m filed after $11.2m of reorganisation charges. Use the filed values for the thesis and P3. Annual statement, Q3 filing.

The stored ROIC therefore needs qualification too: retaining its denominator and tax assumptions but scaling operating profit by 260.6 / 269.4 lowers FY2025 13.12% to about 12.69%. That is a sensitivity, not an independently certified ROIC. Turnover has declined from 0.848× in FY2023 to 0.777×, so the margin improvement does not establish improving asset utilisation. The trailing EPS reconciles as FY2025 $1.22 − prior nine months $0.88 + current nine months $1.08 = $1.42. The tax benefit alone reduces it to $1.36; tariff refunds remain unquantified. No claim is made that 17.64× is fully recurring, or that its historical percentile is known. Current release.

The future entry needs that correct year and the issuer URL above; no tariff amount can be recorded because it is not separately quantified. The finding is preserved here, and the entire position is kept at half-size. This run obeys the brief's proposals-only write boundary.

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake: there is a filed multi-year improvement, not just a rebound narrative; currency is explicitly converted and the return on capital is qualified. The strongest adverse fact is that physical volumes are falling while pricing and exceptional benefits help profit. A larger position would outrun that evidence.

6. The case against

Theses: none. Neither frontier-model pricing nor task-priced software seats drives demand for this equipment.

Dominant risk (financial): Pricing and temporary benefits mask weak physical demand, leaving the manufacturing investment with insufficient enduring returns.

Earliest observable: The next quarterly consolidated volume bridge, filed operating margin and cash conversion, reviewed by 10 November 2026. These arrive within two quarters, so Rule 4 does not halve again.

The Q3 filing attributes sales growth mainly to pricing with volumes lower, while tariff refunds and reduced compensation costs aid profitability. Both earnings and capital employed matter: tying more cash up in foundries can reduce owner returns despite a higher margin. P3 therefore tests margin without requiring revenue to fall too, and the warning tests volume directly.

Total exposure: All three MWA shares in holdings.json have this pot's trade tag; the verified separate human position is zero. The Scan's nominal human-book summary includes those pot shares, so it should not be treated as independent human MWA exposure. This order raises combined ownership from three to seven, remains below 25% of contributed pot capital, and adds to the broader US exposure rather than a large human MWA holding. Scope and sources

The screen covers all 72 watchlist entries: 14 ranked + 58 excluded = 72. The ranking also assesses eight additional human-held Scan names, separately from that count. The actual AI book has £250 contributed and £250 cash, with no open holdings. Pending proposals have no influence on rank.

Read: strategy, pot design, theses, source policy, latest Sweep, latest Review, watchlist, positions, adjustments, holdings, prices, earnings, and signals. The Review found no accepted theses requiring a held-position decision; its older quote marks are not today's ranking inputs.

Inclusion is deliberately broad so basis disagreements remain visible; it does not assert that both screens pass. Percentiles below are local fractions multiplied by 100. A historical percentile on a loss-maker is not accepted as an investable current P/E. No off-universe filing research was started before checking local coverage.

Business ranking

This is a judgment ranking, not a weighted score. Watchlist and human-held names compete on merit. Current pot holdings would affect allocation only; there are none.

RankTickerIn watchlist?Decision and business reasoning

7PDDYesWait. FY2025 operating margin fell while sales grew; the discount alone does not show that spending to retain merchants earns durable returns. T1 may lower internal costs but is not an earnings forecast.

Why the third ticket remains cash

Tradeweb is the nearest alternative. Its Q2 release agrees with local $558.946m revenue and $245.262m operating income. However, rates volume grew 23.1% while rates revenue grew 10.2%; blended fees per million declined 7.2%. Mix accounts for part of that, so it is not proof of competitive failure. It is evidence that “more electronic volume” is insufficient to establish the earnings thesis. I prefer the two small positions over paying for continued platform monetisation before seeing the next quarter's fee conversion. Revisit at the locally scheduled 29 October result if revenue growth catches up without weaker operating margin. This is a business judgment, not a ban caused by uncertified earnings, share price or prior proposals.

Its FY2025 reconciliation also removes $207.078m of Q4 other income and a $9.786m tax-receivable liability adjustment. Local Q4 norm equals attributable income ($324.992m). I do not call 24.64× a verified clean multiple or subtract consolidated pre-tax adjustments directly from after-tax income attributable to common shareholders. The August activity report is encouraging on volume; it does not answer fee yield.

Novo Nordisk is a business-risk wait, not a data refusal. The Q2 filing reports adjusted Q2 sales growth of 7% at constant exchange rates, includes favourable rebate effects, and describes US list-price reductions affecting 2027 cash flow. Lilly's Q2 release reports 48% company revenue growth led by Mounjaro and Zepbound. These are not like-for-like market shares; they show a vigorous substitute supplier while Novo resets pricing. I have not established that unit gains outweigh deteriorating net pricing enough to restore historic returns. T1/T2 do not directly bear on this drug franchise.

RELX: the H1 filing reports 7% underlying revenue growth. Its reported 20.408× versus local historical median 34.1008× is a 40.2% de-rating, with an 8.84th percentile across 181 weeks from 2023-03-31. T2 offers a possible reason: professional workflows need fewer paid seats. The current growth is evidence against an immediate collapse, but not an independently supported answer to that future risk; no “AI moat survives” premise is smuggled into a buy. The earnings uncertainty could be sized; the missing business rebuttal is why I wait.

R&S: the H1 update reports organic sales down 9%, adjusted orders down 10%, EBITDA margin 19.0% and FCF margin 6.4%. Cash improvement is positive, but deliveries are delayed and customers have installation bottlenecks. Its calendar sets 16 September for H1 results. Wait for evidence of conversion; the 144-week post-listing percentile is indicative, not a cycle of business valuation.

Haier: the filed H1 results, as assessed in the latest Sweep, show falling attributable profit and operating cash despite the HVAC integration case. This run's local quarters independently corroborate that direction: H1 attributable income totals RMB10.316bn versus RMB12.033bn, and revenue RMB152.115bn versus RMB156.494bn. The filing's figures are rounded and not identical; I use the local totals for the arithmetic and do not silently merge the two. The new local quote solves coverage, not the business question. Konecranes instead fails the valuation screen at 54.14th percentile, 181 weeks from 2023-03-31.

NVIDIA: the Q2 10-Q describes receivables increasing with extended payment terms on large multi-quarter customer agreements and investment gains. The local screen's lack of a oneOff flag does not make revenue quality self-proving. Customer-financing exposure is my reason to wait here; the human book's 7.37% holding is disclosure, not the rejection criterion.

Hermès: its local one-share cost is above £250 at current EUR/GBP. It remains ranked for business merit, but the cash bound in §4.2a is absolute. No multi-share position is proposed as a way around it.

The remaining names have the business reasons in the ranking. No company was declined merely because a normalised historical series could not be certified. The two orders show how that uncertainty instead changes sizing. Additional cash is not automatically swept into MWA or NFLX: that would undo the deliberate reduction.

model: gpt-6-astra, lane: deepdive, 2026-09-08 21:24, 13m44s, 3,200,686 tokens (168,705 fresh, 3,013,760 cached, 18,221 out), stamped from the session log rather than self-reported

NFLX — Netflix

What it does: Netflix commissions and licenses entertainment and distributes it through its streaming service. Customers pay subscriptions; advertisers pay to reach viewers on its advertising plan.

1. Order

BUY 1 share of NFLX on Nasdaq, limit $76.77, regular session only, valid through 11 September 2026. Currency USD. Cancel if unfilled; this is a proposal, not an executed position.

Halve the usual £125 allocation to £62.50 under §7.2a because the trailing earnings history contains a termination fee that the vendor-normalised data does not reliably remove. One share costs £56.71, leaving £5.79 of that reduced allocation unused. This is 22.68% of contributed capital, within §4.2, with no whole-share exception. The competitive warning has a monthly external observable, so Rule 4 does not require another reduction; global engagement coverage remains a limitation.

Assume IBKR Pro with $1 per US ticket, as required by the brief, and eligible automatic FX at 0.03%. Commission is 1.303% of the $76.77 ticket; FX is about £0.017. Expected entry and first-year holding costs are £0.76 / 1.333%, with no planned first-year sale, ADR custody or UK share stamp duty. An early exit costs extra. Sources: IBKR US commissions, IBKR FX.

Use existing USD or the costed automatic FX route: a separate $2 manual conversion would make entry costs 3.91% before spread and fail §4.1. Two shares lower commission drag to 0.651%, but cost £113.42 and exceed the deliberate half allocation; do not increase the order merely to dilute fees.

Cash after this order alone, including costs: £192.53. Combined with 3 MWA shares, cash remaining is £139.12 after £109.37 of shares and about £1.51 of entry costs. Funding is the actual £250 in positions; no pending draft is counted as a holding. FX and arithmetic use prices, USD per GBP 1.3537. See the complete ranking for the unused budget.

2. Thesis

Netflix can earn from the same distribution service through both subscriptions and advertising, with content expenditure spread across paying audiences in multiple markets. Local annual operating margin rose from 20.62% to 26.71% to 29.49% in FY2023–25, while ROIC rose from 15.20% to 21.24% to 25.78%: that is an operating record rather than a cheap-P/E story. My inference is that the market may be giving insufficient weight to an additional advertising revenue stream on an existing service; whether customers keep giving that service their attention is the unresolved test, not an assumed moat.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At each new monthly Nielsen US Gauge release through 31 March 2027, Netflix's share of total television usage below 7.5% in two consecutive comparable months triggers a re-read. The independently verified May 2026 baseline is 8.0%; this threshold represents a sustained half-point loss, not a company target. It tests attention directly even if price increases keep revenue growing. The May report supplies the baseline; the June report shows why one sports-heavy month is insufficient.

Break: By 31 March 2027, three consecutive comparable monthly releases below 7.0% break this proposal's assumption of a sufficiently durable audience franchise and call for exit under §5.1, even if headline revenue meets guidance. This is my risk threshold, not a statistical claim that US TV measures all Netflix use. Do not join observations across a Nielsen methodology change without a comparable back series: obtain the restatement or record the metric as unavailable and re-review the position. An unavailable series is not a green result.

Quarterly revenue and operating margin are secondary checks, not substitutes for this attention test. No automatic exit is inferred from one weak title or a share-price fall.

4. Review date

22 October 2026, regardless of price. The local next-result date of 20 October is estimated. Check new monthly audience reports when published, and resolve the break assessment by 31 March 2027.

5. Numbers as of today

Local snapshot 2026-09-08 21:22 UTC, regular price struck 20:00 UTC. Extended-hours prices are separate and are not substituted into valuation or sizing.

One-off first: the 10-Q records a $2.8bn WBD termination fee in Q1 2026. Local Q1 norm equals net income at $5.283bn. A clean-looking Scan without a oneOff flag therefore does not certify the earnings.

For a deliberately conservative sensitivity, subtract the entire pre-tax fee, without a tax credit or acquisition-cost add-back, from vendor trailing EPS using Q1 diluted shares 4.298437bn: $3.177 − $2.8bn / 4.298437bn = $2.526, giving 30.40×. This is a stress calculation, not filed recurring EPS: an exact after-tax adjustment has not been established. It is 30.1% below the reported historical median, but that comparison is indicative because the bases differ. I do not claim a recalculated clean percentile. Zero years carry cited NFLX adjustments in the local ledger; this uncertainty halves the order rather than vetoing the business.

Local check: current operating figures agree; the earnings-quality classification does not. The proposal relies on the operating record and the conservative sensitivity, not on $3.18 being wholly recurring. The local floor used EPS of $4.422 in July, unlike today's $3.18; this also cautions against treating its 15.59× floor as a directly comparable normal multiple.

The shareholder letter forecasts roughly $3bn advertising revenue in 2026 and moves comprehensive viewing-hours disclosure to an annual publication in Q1 starting in 2027. Forecasts are not booked earnings; reduced disclosure is a reason for the independent warning.

7532.T check: the purchase is not based on subscriber enthusiasm or a rebound narrative. Capital returns, content economics, the termination-fee sensitivity and external attention data all bear on the decision. Content is an asset that must keep being replenished; high historical margins are not proof that the next slate earns the same return.

6. The case against

Theses: T1, indirectly: cheaper usable AI could reduce production and discovery costs for Netflix and competing entertainment suppliers; no quantified saving is assumed. T2 does not directly apply to a consumer entertainment subscription rather than a task-priced professional seat.

Dominant risk (competitive): YouTube and other entertainment services take viewers' attention before subscription pricing or advertising revenue reveals the loss.

Earliest observable: Nielsen's monthly US television-usage share, The Gauge; the next publication is expected within its monthly cadence, but an exact release date was not verified. May's Netflix 8.0% versus YouTube 13.8% establishes a substantial competing destination. June's sports-driven viewing shifts demonstrate noise, so P3 requires persistence. Nielsen also announces autumn methodology changes; comparability must be checked.

This is a US TV proxy, excluding a complete view of mobile and international use. It can miss damage elsewhere; annual global view-hour reporting is slower, and an advertising forecast cannot answer the competitive objection. T1 could lower competitors' production costs too: the proposal claims no valuation uplift from AI and does not assume that cheaper tools protect Netflix's audience.

Combined exposure: Netflix is already 0.88% of the human book in signals, with 20 shares in holdings. This adds one share to that company exposure, about 0.044% of the £128,916 human-book value, and adds to a book already 66.24% US. It is not one of the book's largest individual positions; overlap is disclosed, not used as a ranking veto.

MWA — Mueller Water Products

What it does: Mueller manufactures valves, hydrants, meters and related equipment for water networks. Utilities, municipalities and distributors buy its products to build, maintain and measure water systems.

1. Order

BUY 3 shares of MWA on NYSE, limit $23.76, regular session only. Currency USD. Valid through 11 September 2026; cancel unfilled shares afterwards rather than chase. This is a proposal for Leo to execute, not a recorded trade.

The usual £125 allocation is halved to £62.50 under §7.2a: the operating-income discrepancy and non-repeat benefits below make the earnings uncertainty material. Three shares deploy £52.66, leaving £9.84 of that reduced allocation unused. No §4.2a exception is needed; the holding would cost 21.06% of the £250 contributed. No further halving under Rule 4: the demand/cash warning is observable at the next quarterly result.

Cost assumption: IBKR Pro, $1 commission per US ticket as required by the brief, with eligible automatic currency conversion at 0.03%. Commission is 1.403% of the $71.28 ticket, FX about £0.016, total entry and first-year holding costs about £0.75 / 1.433%. These are ordinary US shares, with no ADR custody or UK share stamp duty budgeted. No sale is planned in year one; an early sale would add its own costs. Sources: IBKR stock schedule, FX schedule.

This order requires that costed FX route or existing USD. A separate $2 manual conversion would raise entry costs to 4.21% before spread and fail §4.1. Do not place it using that route. Four shares would lower commission drag to 1.052%, but cost £70.21 and breach the deliberate £62.50 allocation; saving that fee percentage does not justify increasing risk.

Cash after this order alone, including estimated costs: £196.59. Together with this run's one-share Netflix proposal, total deployment is £109.37, estimated costs £1.51, and cash left £139.12. Both calculations use prices.json, USD per GBP 1.3537. The ranking explains why the remaining cash is not a third ticket.

2. Thesis

Water-system maintenance provides a recurring use for Mueller's installed manufacturing capacity, while the investment case is that a larger share of sales can become operating cash as that capacity is used. Local FY2023–25 operating margins rose from 10.79% to 16.26% to 18.84%, and ROIC rose from 8.39% to 11.01% to 13.12%, giving this argument more substance than an infrastructure-spending headline. My inference is that the market may be extrapolating weak construction into the whole franchise; I am buying a small stake in demonstrated operating improvement, not assuming that current price increases or tax benefits will repeat.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At the FY2026 release, expected around 5 November (local date is an estimate), either another reported decline in consolidated physical volumes or FY free cash flow at or below 70% of management's adjusted net income triggers a re-read. The first tests whether price is masking demand; the second tests whether the profit is becoming cash. The 70% reference is management's cash-conversion commitment in its Q3 release. If volumes are not quantified, use the explicit direction in the sales bridge; silence is unavailable evidence, not a pass.

Break: By the Q1 FY2027 release, reviewed no later than 28 February 2027, two successive post-entry quarters with declining consolidated volumes and GAAP operating margin below 18% in each break the capacity-return thesis and call for an exit under §5.1. This is my decision threshold, below the locally recorded FY2025 margin, not company guidance. Use filed operating income after reorganisation charges, not the local field if the discrepancy below persists. A missing disclosure triggers review, not an invented result.

4. Review date

10 November 2026, regardless of price; earlier if a warning becomes public. Check again by 28 February 2027 for the two-quarter break.

6. The case against

Theses: none.

Dominant risk (financial): physical demand weakens enough that the expanded manufacturing asset base stops earning its improved returns, while pricing temporarily hides that deterioration.

Earliest observable: the next quarterly sales bridge's volume direction, followed by the FY cash-flow statement, around November 2026; company results. P3 tests both before waiting for a collapse in annual EPS.

The Q3 release already attributes sales growth mainly to price with slightly lower volumes. Temporary income and the local operating-income classification make the margin improvement less persuasive than the screen suggests. This can remain a cash-generative business while being a poor purchase if factory economics fade; the small order does not resolve that objection.

Combined exposure: no MWA position appears in holdings.json. This adds a new company, but adds US exposure to a human book already 66.24% US in signals.json; it does not diversify the listing geography.

Decision: no security order. Retain £250. MWA is my strongest research candidate, but its current earnings still need a bridge separating recurring operations from temporary benefits. PDD is second: its operating performance is stronger than the decline in net profit suggests, but I cannot yet underwrite the earnings after compliance costs. What this does: The pot keeps its funded cash available for a later investment or the standing order. It acquires no shares and makes no claim to earn a particular cash interest rate.

Inputs: the latest Sweep, latest Review, Scan, strategy, design, source policy, and standing theses. Coverage was checked locally before company research. Previous proposals are not holdings or reservations on cash.

1. Order

HOLD CASH £250. Security quantity: zero. Cash deployed: £0. Cash left idle: £250. Transaction costs: £0. No trade is instructed by this document.

positions.json, generated 09:46:27 UTC, records one £250 contribution and no holdings. The ordinary allocation could support two £125 positions; none passes the full investment assessment below. I assessed the remaining candidates after MWA rather than stopping after its first slot. The fresh-name preference has no allocation effect because the pot owns nothing.

Affordability is not MWA's problem. A hypothetical, not instructed, seven-share ticket at $24 would deploy £124.18 using USD/GBP 1.3529. Eight shares would deploy £141.92, above the ordinary £125 cap. At seven shares, IBKR's fixed US $1 commission is 0.595% of the $168 ticket; at eight it would be 0.521%, an improvement that does not justify breaching §4.2. A separate manual FX conversion has a $2 minimum, making the two fees £2.22 or 1.786% before the variable market spread. The published automatic-conversion alternative adds approximately 0.03% instead, where available; it is not assumed to be Leo's account arrangement. The manual-fee scenario leaves £123.60 of the pot after ticket and fees. Thus neither the $1 fee nor unused cash is the reason to reject MWA. These are entry-cost illustrations, not a complete executable order or an assumed first-year sale. Sources: local FX, IBKR stocks, IBKR FX.

One INTU share is £245.92 at the local quote. §4.2a permits that concentration if affordable after costs; I have not excluded it for costing more than £125. Its business-risk assessment fails first. Nor have I used existing exposure in Leo's human book to penalize a rank.

2. Thesis

The best available industrial candidate has demonstrated operating improvement, but the newest earnings combine that improvement with benefits whose persistence I cannot establish. Several alternatives have a real business case, yet their apparently cheap multiples depend on incomplete earnings reconciliation, weakening demand, or an unresolved mechanism of customer displacement. Retaining cash until those specific questions are answered is preferable to treating a low historical percentile as the missing investment thesis.

Why this avoids the 7532.T mistake: infrastructure replacement, cheaper AI, recovering consumption and merchant-platform scale are leads, not proofs of returns. I checked margins across periods, the capital employed, current operating evidence, currency units and the purchase filter; a compelling category story does not compensate for a denominator I cannot defend. The opportunity cost of waiting remains real, particularly for MWA and PDD.

3. Falsifier

These tests reopen the cash decision; they are not sell rules for positions that do not exist.

Warning: Reassess immediately when a sourced bridge establishes an investible earnings base for MWA or Tradeweb, or a company/regulator disclosure resolves a ranked candidate's stated obstacle. Do not wait for the share price to rise. If that happens before the dated reviews below, holding all cash deserves an immediate re-read.

Break: The all-cash decision ceases to be justified once a candidate passes the local valuation and data checks, has a business thesis independent of its multiple, a dated warning and break addressing its dominant risk, and a whole-share ticket satisfying cash and cost limits. A new proposal is then required; this document does not authorize a purchase automatically. A fresh Scan instruction under §11.1 is independently controlling.
