MWA: the best case is stronger than a generic refusal, but not yet enough. The Q2 release reports $384.4m sales, $80.4m GAAP operating profit and 20.9% margin, with pricing, volume and manufacturing efficiency contributing. This demonstrates that improvement predates Q3's refunds. Against that, six-month free cash flow was $16.5m versus $47.3m, so earnings improvement did not yet imply matching cash conversion. Local Q2 opinc is $84.8m, the adjusted figure, while net income of $59.1m agrees. I use the filed GAAP subtotal.

The annual filed statement gives GAAP operating income of $127.4m, $181.7m and $260.6m for FY2023–25, against local $137.6m, $213.8m and $269.4m. These reconcile through $10.2m, $32.1m and $8.8m restructuring/impairment charges. Correct margins are 9.99%, 13.82%, 18.23%, rather than local 10.79%, 16.26%, 18.84%. Revenue and net income agree. The local FY2025 ROIC of 13.12% inherits an operating-profit basis caveat and is not a separately verified GAAP return.

For Q3, the 10-Q reconciles local $91.8m operating profit to $80.6m GAAP after $11.2m charges; the issuer's adjusted subtotal is instead $94.9m after another $3.1m adjustment. It also attributes improvements to non-recurring tariff refunds and lower incentive/FX expense, with consolidated volume declining. I found no amount isolating the refunds. Therefore none of these three operating-profit subtotals is automatically a refund-free baseline.

The Q3 release identifies a $0.06 adjusted-EPS benefit from the one-time tax item. Removing it from adjusted quarterly EPS of $0.50 gives $0.44, still including any tariff benefits; this is not a clean GAAP EPS estimate. The local TTM EPS of $1.42 and normalized $1.46915 should not be described as fully cleaned. No Scan oneOff flag on MWA proves otherwise. The annual improvement is meaningful, but I cannot yet establish the current repeatable earnings base that this purchase would capitalize. That is my judgement for waiting, not a claim that the business has failed.

PDD: acknowledge the favourable evidence. Its 24 August release agrees with local Q2 revenue RMB112.358bn, operating profit RMB27.764bn and attributable income RMB27.182bn. Operating profit rose 8%, while attributable income fell 12%; cash from operations rose to RMB25.7bn from RMB21.6bn. Local diluted quarterly EPS is RMB18.44 versus filed RMB18.45, a disclosed small discrepancy, not a reason to manufacture a different USD multiple. The Scan's oneOff wording only says recurring P/E is above its floor; it does not diagnose a particular gain. My concern is prospective compliance economics: the Commission's €200m decision requires operational remedies, not just payment. I did not retrieve confirmation of the plan's submission or acceptance. The group disclosure does not separately establish Temu's post-remedy margin. This leaves no sufficiently supported account of what the market is missing; it does not prove the entire group is unprofitable.

RELX and Intuit: a declared thesis must affect the conclusion. T2 directly challenges paid workflow units, while T1 may reduce model input costs without preserving seat prices. RELX's H1 release reports 7% underlying revenue growth and a 35.5% adjusted operating margin. Local recurring P/E is 20.45×, approximately 40.0% below the stored headline median of 34.1008×; that comparison is context with differing earnings bases, not an exact recurring de-rating. Its current percentile/window is in the table. A plausible market discount is weaker ownership of the customer interface as agents handle research tasks. I have no paid-unit evidence demonstrating that this concern is wrongly priced.

Outside its filings, Harvey reports more than 2,400 customers across more than 70 countries at retrieval. This is a vendor's aggregate claim, not a count of displaced Lexis seats, and its publication cadence is unspecified. It establishes a substitute to investigate, not a sell signal. A quarterly check of that page is a research cadence, not a promised quarterly disclosure. If that remained the only dominant-risk observable, Rule 4 would halve the allocation rather than allowing full size behind a leverage falsifier.

Intuit's FY2026 release reports $16.46 GAAP EPS versus local $16.47; local annual financials still stop at FY2025. Revenue rose 14% and operating income 20%, while total US TurboTax units fell from 39.9m to 39.0m and TurboTax revenue rose 7%. This does not prove AI caused the unit loss, but it directly refutes using revenue growth alone to test customer retention. The annual unit observation is slow; the 17 September investor day may help but is not a promised new unit disclosure. I found no usable fresh IRS adoption series and do not assume Direct File is currently an expanding competitor. An eventual proposal needs a dated external observation or the smaller Rule 4 size, plus an argument that the discount is wrong.

Tradeweb and AMSC: normalization is not verified by the field name. Tradeweb's Q4 release identifies $205.4m of Canton gains. Local Q4 norm equals ni at $324.992m, so that series cannot establish profit stripped of the gain. Local annual operating profit of $845.124m also differs from filed $835.3m, giving 41.18% versus 40.70% on the same revenue. I have not attached the old percentile to a newly invented denominator. AMSC's 10-K records a $118.4m deferred-tax benefit against local annual net income of $133.809m; local normalized profit is $136.312m. Its low headline and recurring percentiles are not evidence of cheap operating earnings.

The latest operating evidence elsewhere:

  • R&S's preliminary H1 report shows sales CHF179.2m and EBITDA CHF34m, down 13% and 23%, despite CHF357.9m backlog. The 7 September announcement confirms the CEO's immediate departure and interim CFO leadership. Its local annual record is older evidence. HISTORY_FROM already excludes the pre-business SPAC history; I found no new missing cutoff to report.
  • Haier's local H1 sums are RMB152.115bn revenue and RMB10.316bn attributable income, down 2.80% and 14.27% against the same local quarters of 2025. They agree to rounding with the issuer release. The Sweep's 26.8% filed gross-margin figure conflicts with that release's 27.2%; direct HKEX PDF retrieval failed in this run, so the filed percentage is an unreverified Sweep finding, not my established figure. I use neither to make a margin-improvement claim. Local capital data are absent. Its new local coverage resolves the price-fetch prerequisite, not the investment question.
  • Lululemon's Q2 release reports comparable sales down 9%, and a $134.5m tariff refund adding 5.6 percentage points to operating margin. Local operating profit/revenue agrees with its 18.8% margin, but excluding the refund leaves approximately 13.2%. 6. The case against

Theses: T2 bears on RELX, Intuit and Wiley because agents can change paid workflow/customer economics; T1 bears on their model input costs and Xiaomi's model activity, without guaranteeing margins. Neither supplies the business case for MWA, PDD, Haier or R&S.

Dominant risk (accounting): The leading candidates' apparently cheap earnings are not yet demonstrated to be repeatable on a comparable basis, so buying the current screen could capitalize temporary gains as durable profit.

Earliest observable: A filing-based bridge of MWA's tariff/tax benefits or Tradeweb's investment gains can be checked as soon as located; the next dated company reports offer further evidence. The current inability to isolate these amounts is itself information, not a zero assumption. P3 directly reopens the decision when that accounting evidence changes.

The strongest argument against holding cash is that MWA already improved margins before the latest benefits and PDD's current operating profit and cash flow are growing. Demanding excessive precision can miss an attractive business, and a small funded pot cannot wait indefinitely for perfect disclosure. I nevertheless cannot supply the business-and-valuation argument with enough confidence today; the next review should resolve these named gaps rather than silently tightening the rules again. Rule 4 is not waived: an eventual order resting on an undated or more-than-two-quarter dominant-risk observable defaults to half allocation, or must explicitly defend full size in P1. A smaller ticket does not repair a failed local earnings comparison.

Combined exposure: no purchase changes Leo's human holdings. signals.json records a £129,357 human book, 66.18% US, with Google 10.53%, Microsoft 8.84%, Apple 8.59% and Nvidia 7.50%. Leaving the pot's £250 idle therefore makes little difference to the total investment exposure; the cash decision is about the pot's next purchase, not a forecast that markets will fall. There is no overlap penalty in the ranking.

Only this proposal record was written. Data discrepancies and unavailable sources are documented here because this lane permits writes only under pot/proposals/; no source data, watchlist, book, design document or earlier proposal was changed.

model: gpt-6-astra, lane: deepdive, 2026-09-08 00:03, 8m38s, 2,253,110 tokens (163,919 fresh, 2,076,544 cached, 12,647 out), stamped from the session log rather than self-reported

No order — hold £250

8 September 2026, 00:08 UTC. This run stands on its own. Earlier proposals are unexecuted drafts, and did not constrain the ranking.

1. Order

No BUY, SELL or TRIM. Keep the full £250 in cash under strategy §4.4. Capital deployed: £0. Trading costs: £0. The actual book has one £250 contribution dated 4 September and no holdings. The Scan contains no standing-order instruction.

Both potential £125 allocations were considered. The decision is that no researched candidate currently combines a sufficiently supported business case with a trustworthy valuation comparison; it is not a decision to reserve money for older drafts or stop after considering one ticket.

Costs would not prevent the leading US candidates from being considered. For illustration only, at $24, seven MWA shares would cost £124.00 at local GBP/USD 1.3548. IBKR UK fixed pricing has a $1 US minimum, equivalent to £0.74 or 0.595% of that ticket; eligible automatic FX conversion adds approximately £0.04 at 0.03%, giving about 0.625% entry commission plus FX. Eight shares would reduce commission to 0.521%, and ten to 0.417%, but cost £141.72 and £177.15 respectively: both exceed the £125 concentration allocation. Idle cash does not waive §4.2 when seven shares already fit. One TW share at the local $106.20 would cost £78.39, with commission of 0.942%; two would exceed £125. These are sizing comparisons, not orders or complete first-year cost quotes. Sources: local rates and prices, IBKR stock schedule, IBKR automatic FX terms.

2. Why cash wins this run

The strongest leads remain MWA's water-network equipment, Tradeweb's electronic markets and RELX's information businesses. The first two have operating evidence worth following, but their local earnings labels make the screen look cleaner than the filings support; RELX requires an argument about displacement that its low multiple cannot supply. This is the 7532.T test: neither necessary infrastructure, trading automation nor AI-enabled information products is enough without checking earnings, capital productivity, the price paid and the mechanism that could reverse the apparent improvement.

The candidates come from the newest Sweep, 2325.T and LRE.L, together with every unique ticker in the current Scan. The newest Review was also read. NJS now has local EPS and five P/E bands: its Sweep-era coverage gap has closed. GWRE still has no peBands and was excluded before company research, as the brief requires. Every other considered name has EPS and P/E bands.

MWA — first to revisit, but the margin bridge is incomplete

Mueller manufactures valves, hydrants, meters and related equipment used by water utilities and construction customers. It earns money from selling those products and associated services. The Q3 release reports 4.1% sales growth, driven by pricing while volumes were slightly lower; tariff refunds and reduced incentive compensation also helped profit. Management raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $367m–$372m. That is evidence of current earnings, but does not isolate repeatable improvement from temporary assistance.

Theses: none. Dominant risk: financial — temporary price/cost and expense benefits are being capitalised as a lasting margin improvement. The local absence of a oneOff flag does not settle this question. The filing bridge in P5 corrects the margin, and still shows improvement: rejecting the local label does not erase that improvement. However, I could not quantify a clean tariff-refund and compensation bridge from the retrieved disclosures. I therefore do not claim that the stored 16.30× “recurring” P/E establishes the price of sustainable earnings.

The reason to wait is the combination of unproven margin persistence and an inadequately reconciled denominator, not a new rule that any data discrepancy prohibits a purchase. At the next result, check volume, price, tariff refunds, incentive compensation and GAAP operating profit separately. An EBITDA guidance miss alone would detect the problem too late if temporary benefits keep the headline green. All interpretation above is this run's judgement.

TW — the one-off is substantially larger than the Scan's adjustment

Tradeweb runs electronic markets where institutional investors and dealers trade bonds, derivatives and other instruments. It earns transaction fees, subscriptions and data revenue.

Theses: T2, because automating trading workflows changes how execution is purchased; T1 is a possible input-cost tailwind, not evidence of a moat. Dominant risk: competitive — more automated volume monetises at lower fees. In Q2, revenue grew 9.0% against ADV growth of 18.2%; cash-credit fees per million fell 11.4%, and rates-derivative fees fell 10.3%. Management attributes much of this to mix. The adjusted EBITDA margin was 54.4% versus 54.2%, so the report does not establish competitive displacement; it establishes a monetisation question which volume alone cannot answer. Source: Q2 release.

Q4 2025 included $205.4m of Canton Coin gains, while local quarterly norm equals reported net income. Company-adjusted trailing EPS can be bridged to approximately $3.79, implying 28.02×, rather than local normEps of $4.18 and 25.41×. The calculation and its different accounting basis are in P5. This is not proof TW is expensive; it means its stored recurring percentile is not a verified percentile of earnings excluding that gain. I have not established a separate business reason to buy now while overlooking both that issue and weaker fees per unit.

REL.L — cheapness may be T2 being priced

RELX sells risk analytics, legal research tools, scientific information and exhibition services. Theses: T2 directly bears on legal and scientific workflows; T1 may lower AI input costs for both RELX and substitutes. Dominant risk: secular — agents reduce the value of paid research seats.

Local reported P/E is 20.58×, versus its 34.10× reported-history median, a 39.7% discount; the comparison uses the same reported basis. Local recurring P/E is 20.43×. These are observations, not an attribution of the entire discount to AI. My hypothesis is that the market is discounting weaker long-run pricing and customer economics, of which T2 is one plausible cause.

There is evidence against immediate displacement: H1 Legal underlying revenue grew 10% and adjusted operating profit grew 13%. But growth does not separate units, price and AI attach, so it does not establish that the long-run discount is wrong. Source: RELX H1 filing. Outside RELX, Harvey reported more than 25,000 customer-built agents on 25 March 2026: Harvey announcement. That is substitute adoption, not a count of lost Lexis customers. Its publication cadence is unscheduled, and it supplies no causal crosswalk to paid RELX seats.

I cannot presently write the required early, dated displacement test or an evidence-backed rebuttal of that discount. Rule 4 would halve the allocation if a proposal otherwise cleared; halving does not supply the missing Rule 5 argument. RELX is therefore deferred on the evidence, not automatically excluded for belonging to T2, and not rejected because an older draft exists.

3. What would change this decision

These are research conditions, not retroactive sell rules for old proposals and not automatic buys.

NameEarliest useful checkWhat must be resolved
MWAFY2026 release, locally estimated 5 November; review by 6 November 2026Reconcile GAAP and adjusted margins over comparable periods, quantify temporary benefits where disclosed, and show the earnings base after them. Use volume and cost evidence, not only the EBITDA guidance.
TWNext quarterly result, locally dated 29 October; review by 30 October 2026Bridge operating earnings without investment marks, establish a comparable valuation history, and test fees per unit independently of market share. A further fee decline must not require falling share as a second condition.
REL.LRevisit research by 23 October 2026; this is a chosen deadlineFind customer/seat retention or usage-to-payment evidence and dated external adoption observations. Revenue growth alone cannot disprove T2.
RSGN.SWFull H1 results on 16 September; review 17 September 2026Establish delivery conversion and the margin outlook. The preliminary release has sales down 13% and EBITDA down 23%, despite positive cash flow.
WLY, INTU, NFLXAt the next deep-dive, or sooner if reconciled filings become availableRefresh and reconcile current earnings before attaching a percentile to a clean denominator. For the workflow/information names, also address T2.

Company timing for R&S comes from its H1 update. Other stated local earnings dates come from prices.json; an estimated date is not a company confirmation. The Review reports R&S's immediate CEO departure, but its linked announcement failed to open in this run. I do not rely on that unrefreshed report to reject it: the retrieved operating update already supports waiting.

4. Review date

9 September 2026, regardless of prices, at the next available deep-dive assessment. Reconsider earlier if a clean earnings reconciliation becomes available. This is a recommendation to keep cash today, not an instruction to remain in cash until November.

5. Numbers and local verification

Snapshot: prices.json, fetched 2026-09-07 23:54:20 UTC; signals.json, generated 23:51:17 UTC, referring to that earlier fetch; earnings.json; holdings.json; and positions.json, generated 23:55:23 UTC. Prices and Scan are separate snapshots. US regular-session quotes used here are from 4 September; the quoted European and Japanese listings are from 7 September. Neither an updated file timestamp nor an extended-hours flag is a new regular-session trade.

The MWA annual margin improvement survives the correction, but its level and historical consistency must not be described using mixed GAAP and pre-charge subtotals. Additional date-quality finding: RSGN.SW's stored low date is 11 September 2026, after this assessment. It may be a week-ending label on an incomplete bar, but it cannot be described as a low already traded on that date. Its history begins after the de-SPAC, so no unhandled pre-business history was established in this run.

Run-wide ranking

1. Order

BUY 7 shares of MWA on the New York Stock Exchange, approximately £124.29 of the £125 allocation, DAY limit @ $24.00. Currency USD. The allocation remainder is £0.71; after this order and its estimated FX charge, £125.53 of pot cash remains for the second instruction.

Expected first-year costs, assuming a GBP-funded Trading 212 Stocks ISA: £0 commission, £0 custody, £0 UK stamp duty on this US share, no ADR fee, and about £0.19 one-way FX cost at 0.15%. Total expected cost is about 0.15% of the ticket, below the 2% ceiling. Trading 212 states that custody and platform fees are zero and its FX fee is 0.15% (cost disclosure, FX method); HMRC says foreign shares bought outside the UK do not normally attract Stamp Duty or SDRT (HMRC).

2. Thesis

Mueller sells valves, hydrants, metering and leak-detection equipment used to keep North American water networks operating, a replacement and upgrade market in which failure costs and product qualification matter. Four complete local years show revenue rising each year, GAAP operating margin widening from 10.1% to 18.8%, and FY2025 ROIC reaching 13.1%, while Q3 FY2026 still delivered 4.1% sales growth and a 20.4% GAAP operating margin (earnings.json, prices.json, Q3 release). The market appears to treat the improvement as a temporary pricing cycle; what it may be missing is that foundry investment, portfolio work and the faster-growing Water Management business have changed the earnings base as utilities continue replacing ageing infrastructure.

3. Falsifier

Warning: At the FY2026 result currently estimated for 5 November 2026, trigger a full re-read if net sales are below management's $1.470bn lower bound, adjusted EBITDA is below $367m, or free cash flow is no more than 70% of adjusted net income. Any miss is the first hard evidence that pricing and execution are not carrying into the full year; it is a warning, not an automatic sale (company outlook, local result date).

Break: At the Q2 FY2027 filing, to be checked no later than 7 May 2027, put the position under §5.1 if trailing-twelve-month GAAP operating margin is below 17.0% while trailing-twelve-month revenue growth is below 3.0%. That combination would show that tariff refunds, compensation timing and pricing produced a peak rather than a durable reset in a growing business; it directly tests the dominant risk (current filing and baseline).

4. Review date

6 November 2026, regardless of price, the day after the locally estimated FY2026 result.

Local check: agree on the decision, with a disclosed qualification. The local annual series is used for filed history and the company filing for newer Q3 evidence. Local trailing EPS is current through June 2026 and carries no epsStale or oneOff annotation, but the filing says higher pricing and non-recurring tariff refunds helped Q3 gross margin and a one-time tax benefit reduced the full-year tax-rate guidance. The refund is not quantified, so it cannot be removed cleanly; both reported and normalized local multiples still pass, and P3 tests whether the margin survives.

6. The case against

Dominant risk (financial): The margin expansion may be a temporary peak built on pricing, non-recurring tariff refunds and lower incentive compensation while physical volumes remain weak.

Earliest observable: The FY2026 result, locally estimated for 5 November 2026, will print sales, adjusted EBITDA and free-cash-flow conversion against the $1.470bn, $367m and 70% thresholds in P3 (company outlook, prices.json).

Water Flow Solutions sales fell 0.6% in Q3, inventory rose from $328.7m to $379.8m over nine months and absorbed $59.9m of cash, and foundry capital spending is increasing. If pricing support reverses while inflation, residential construction or municipal budgets soften, a low P/E capitalises peak earnings and both earnings and the multiple can contract (Q3 filing).

Combined exposure: MWA is not in the human book, so the existing name weight is 0%; the order does add another North American industrial exposure to a book already 66.27% US by market value (signals.json).

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake again: this is not a generic infrastructure rebound. The case starts with four filed years of revenue and GAAP margin, explicit capital-return and cash evidence, uses valuation only as a gate, and makes temporary margin support the subject of both falsifier tiers.

6. The case against

Dominant risk (financial): Tradeweb's network may be adding notional trading volume faster than economic value as product mix, volume discounts and client bargaining power compress fee capture.

Earliest observable: The Q3 filing on 29 October 2026 will disclose transaction-fee growth, ADV growth and variable fees per million against P3's 15-point and 10% thresholds (Q2 filing and disclosure cadence, prices.json).

In Q2, ADV rose 18.2% but transaction fees grew only 8.3%; total variable fees per million fell 7.2%, cash-credit fees fell 11.4%, and growth skewed toward lower-fee short-tenor derivatives, European credit and portfolio trading. August ADV still grew 13.7%, but its high-yield TRACE share was 8.3% versus 8.5% in Q2, so the newest volume release does not settle whether economics are compounding with activity. Impressive volume and share statistics can therefore coexist with structurally weaker monetisation, while the two missing local capital-return measures make the quality case less complete than MWA's (Q2 filing, August activity).

Combined exposure: TW is not in the human book, so the existing name weight is 0%; the order adds another US financial-market infrastructure exposure to a book already 66.27% US by market value (signals.json).

Why this is not the 7532.T mistake again: this is not a generic bet on electronic trading or volatility. The case starts with four filed years of revenue and GAAP margin progression, admits that two capital-return measures are unavailable, uses valuation only as a gate, and tests the exact weakness in the latest filing—whether volume becomes transaction revenue while electronic market share continues to rise.

Local opinc is CHF77.334m, or 18.6% of revenue, while the annual report states CHF79.2m EBIT and a 19.1% margin; the official audited EBIT is used when describing FY2025 and the local series is retained, labelled, in the ranking and table. The Scan carries no oneOff or epsStale annotation for RSGN.SW.

6. The case against

The share may be cheap because earnings are already rolling over. H1 adjusted order intake fell 10%, sales fell 13%, EBITDA fell 23%, and management now expects FY2026 revenue of CHF410m–CHF420m— roughly flat with FY2025 and below its mid-term organic growth range. Utility customers have excess inventory and installation bottlenecks, while the higher power-transformer mix takes longer to produce; backlog can therefore look reassuring for years before becoming cash, and factory delays would hurt both revenue and margins (H1 update).

The accounting also deserves scepticism. Much of FY2025's reported growth came from the first full year of Kyte Powertech, bought for CHF256.9m; CHF180.7m of acquisition goodwill was written directly against equity under Swiss GAAP FER, and its theoretical residual goodwill was still CHF131.4m at year-end. The report's own theoretical capitalization view shows CHF39.7m of 2025 goodwill amortisation that does not pass through reported profit, while copper and aluminium input prices were already rising (2025 annual report).

Finally, this is a short listed history—only 179 locally priced weeks—and a small SIX line where the bid/ask spread and a second commission can matter more than the modelled fees. The strongest reason not to buy is that the market may correctly see peak transformer margins, acquisition- flattered growth and an expensive capacity build meeting normalized utility demand. The 12.70× multiple is only the gate RSGN.SW passed; it does not make that cycle risk disappear.

2. Thesis

NVIDIA's earnings quality clears Leo's test: filed annual revenue expanded from $27.0bn in FY2023 to $215.9bn in FY2026 while operating margin rose from 20.7% to 60.4%, rather than profit being supplied by a one-off (local earnings). The market may still be underestimating how quickly simultaneous demand from frontier labs, cloud providers and physical-AI workloads can turn the Rubin ramp into earnings, with management guiding Q3 revenue to $108.0bn ±2% even while assuming no China Data Center compute revenue (Q2 results).

This is not the 7532.T mistake again: the case is not a rebound narrative or a local-currency share price. It is supported by four filed years of accelerating USD revenue and sustained high margins, a current multiple below the company's own point-in-time range, and an explicit acknowledgement of China, customer concentration and cyclicality rather than treating them as afterthoughts.

3. Falsifier

The thesis is false if NVIDIA reports Q3 FY2027 GAAP gross margin below 70.0%. That would be at least 4.0 percentage points below management's 74.0% guide midpoint and would show that the economics of the Rubin ramp are deteriorating materially despite the guided revenue growth (Q2 results).

GameStop earns this small position because Q1 FY2026 sales grew 14.0%, gross margin expanded to 40.7% from 34.5%, and adjusted operating income rose to $140.5m from $27.5m as collectibles sales grew 65.0%—an operating improvement, not merely investment income (Q1 release, 10-Q). This is not 7532.T again: the case is grounded in filed margin and mix data, strips the $268.4m unrealized eBay derivative gain out of normalized earnings, pays the explicit GBP/USD cost rather than hand-waving currency, and is falsified at the next quarterly disclosure rather than by a rebound story (10-Q, prices.json).

Local Q1 opinc is $138.7m versus SEC GAAP $143.3m because the local figure excludes the $4.6m impairment reversal; local Q1 normalized income is $178.817m versus company-adjusted net income of $179.3m, so the official $179.3m is used for that quarter while local normEps remains the pipeline-consistent TTM denominator. Local FY2025 opinc is $285.9m versus SEC GAAP $232.1m—the exact $53.8m difference is the filed impairment charge—so GAAP margins above use the SEC filing and normalized earnings use the clearly labelled local series (earnings.json, FY2025 10-K, Q1 10-Q).

6. The case against

Do not buy this if you want a predictable compounder. Filed revenue fell from $5.2728b in FY2023 to $3.6299b in FY2025, only the latest of those three years had positive GAAP operating income, and Q1's recovery was concentrated in collectibles while hardware fell 3.4% and software fell 13.0% (FY2025 10-K, Q1 10-Q). The headline 13.60× P/E flatters the business because $268.4m of Q1 profit was an unrealized eBay derivative gain; even the normalized 16.50× multiple rests on a 23.65× floor struck from only 30 positive-earnings weeks after years of losses, so this is a thin historical anchor, not proof of cheapness (prices.json, Q1 10-Q).

Most importantly, GameStop is becoming a concentrated capital-allocation vehicle: it held 4,710 Bitcoin, posted $983.3m collateral against eBay derivatives, remains committed to an eBay transaction after eBay rejected its $55.5b proposal, and has agreed to retire $1.4b of convertible debt for an as-yet-undetermined number of new shares (Q1 10-Q, eBay rejection, GameStop proposal, debt exchange 8-K). The strongest reason to reject the order is therefore that the apparent retail turnaround may be real but the shareholder outcome is increasingly dominated by Ryan Cohen's opaque, volatile investment and dilution decisions; £125 is sized as an experiment in that uncertainty, not as confidence that it has gone away.

Sweep — 11 September 2026, 23:55 UTC

Candidates only. Reads the 23:46 UTC prices and 23:42 UTC signals snapshots. Previous sweep: 17:04 today, which closed by naming the book's total absence of energy and real-asset exposure as "a thread for a future sweep to research properly". This run picks up that thread and reports what the research actually found, which is not what the thread expected.

1. Where the world is

Observation — what we hold. Oil is still the hardest-running series in the macro block: WTI $99.99, +7.48% over 7 days, +23.06% over the month, +74.44% year to date. US 10-year 4.975% (+18.82% ytd), 5-year 4.791% (+28.14% ytd). Gold $4,390, −12.09% over six months. S&P 500 7,656.98, −0.22% on the week. Hang Seng 24,805.63, −6.00% over a year (prices.json, macro block).

Observation — what we do not hold, and it is the bigger number. The macro block carries WTI and nothing else in energy. Going outside it: Dutch TTF front-month gas is €81.50/MWh, +152% over a year and within a euro of its 52-week high of €82.05, while US Henry Hub is $2.82/mmbtu, −3.9% over a year; Brent is $104.42, +57.3% (all Yahoo, provisional — see §4, these are macro series and belong in the macro block, not in the equity watchlist). The mechanism is not the crude headline. The Strait of Hormuz carries roughly a fifth of global LNG trade and Qatari flows are substantially blocked, with Europe rebuilding storage into winter from a level below its historical norm (Kpler, Euronews — press, cited for narrative only; the storage percentage itself I could not source cleanly, see §4). Marine war-risk premiums for Hormuz transits have gone from roughly 0.25% of hull value before the war to 7.5–10% (S&P Global, The National). The FOMC meets 16 September with market-implied odds of a hike around half to two-thirds (CME FedWatch as reported; the July decision held at 3.50–3.75% with three dissents in favour of raising, Fed minutes).

Inference. The single widest dislocation in the world right now is not oil, it is the spread between European and American gas — a factor of roughly ten on an energy-equivalent basis, from a series our seventeen do not contain. Two things follow that the oil headline does not give you. First, this is a cost shock localised to Europe, so it argues against buying European energy-intensive manufacturing on weakness, and that cuts against the standing diversify-out-of-the-US bias rather than with it — worth saying plainly, because the bias is meant to be a preference and not a reflex. Second, the beneficiary is the producer sitting on $2.82 gas competing against one paying €81.50, which is a US position; the book is already 66.88% US, so that idea has to win on merits, and below I only re-look at one we already carry rather than adding another American name.

On the energy void the last sweep flagged: I researched it and the honest answer is that the obvious vehicles have already run. Saipem is +82.6% over a year and Subsea7 +58.3% (NOK 321.6 against a 52-week high of 351) — both near highs (§3). Buying offshore energy services at $100 spot crude, after an 80% move, on the argument that capex must follow, is the 7532.T shape almost exactly: a real macro story, a stock that has already discounted it, and no work done on mid-cycle earnings. So the void stays open this week by choice.

2. Leo's reading

Unchanged — no new entry and no new file in pot/reading/; all four saved articles are listed in the index, so nothing is invisible to this lane.

  • Burry's two Hong Kong pieces (VIE exposure as a sizing decision; Hang Seng Tech de-rating, not deterioration) — unchanged since 17:04 today. ^HSI −6.00% over a year keeps that read intact.
  • Burry's 9 September Trading Post remains paywalled beyond its introduction. Secondary write-ups characterise it as reduced exposure with no thesis change; I am not adopting a view from a summary of a post I cannot read.
  • The two Kind: method pieces (Djukanovic on margins, Ivan Li on convexity) are absorbed. Neither argues against a written rule — §2.4 already carries ROIC, gross profit ÷ total assets and asset turnover. Nothing to re-argue.

3. Candidates

Read against book: 66.88% US, and by sector Technology 40.16% + Communication Services 19.19% ≈ 59%, against Industrials 7.25%, Financial Services 7.66%, and no Energy line at all (residual tail 0.76%). All prices below are Yahoo and provisional until the pipeline carries them.

1WRT1V.HE — WärtsiläHelsinkiAll-time-high H1 order intake €4,934m (+23%), order book €8,976m (+13%), Q2 book-to-bill 1.83, comparable operating margin 13.7%, and service is €1,642m of €3,004m H1 net sales (company release) — yet the shares are €28.90, 27% below the 52-week high of €39.63, because both divisions guided demand only "similar" for the next 12 months. Sells the engines into a shipbuilding order book at a 17-year high rather than building hulls. Adds Industrials, non-US.The order book converts at ≥13% comparable margin with service holding above half of sales, and the Energy "similar" guide proves a pause rather than the peak. Against it: gas at €81.50 is a headwind to European gas-fired generation, which is a real part of that Energy division.
2LRE.L — Lancashire — re-lookLondonAlready on the watchlist. War-risk pricing has gone up ~30–40× and Lancashire is the purest listed writer of it, with H1'26 profit after tax $141.7m (+30%), annualised RoE 19.6%, undiscounted combined ratio 90.8%, diluted book value $5.92/share, Middle East losses stated as "not material" and the MV Dali reserve taken to full policy limits, capping that downside (H1 2026 RNS). The shares are 620.5p, +2.2% over a year while Beazley is +64.4% on the same event.The divergence is not yet an argument. 620.5p at GBP/USD 1.3529 is $8.40 against $5.92 of book — ~1.42× book, which a 19.6% RoE roughly justifies, so this is "has not moved", not "is cheap". Second-order, slow, and not what is being written about. Adds US, which the book does not need — it wins only on merits.CF's own filed realised nitrogen price and natural gas cost per tonne show the spread reaching the P&L rather than being competed away, and European curtailments are announced rather than assumed.
4SPM.MI — SaipemMilanThe only name here that fills the Energy void. Absorbing Subsea7 to form Saipem7 (Milan + Oslo listings); Subsea7's own Q2 shows backlog $13.6bn, book-to-bill 1.1×, adjusted EBITDA $471m +31%, margin 24% (company release); the EU Phase 2 decision is due 26 November 2026 (ACCC is also at Phase 2). Watch, do not buy. €4.313, +82.6% over a year, against a 52-week high of €4.82.A merger break or a crude reversal takes it back towards mid-cycle earnings, and Saipem's own filed net debt and cash conversion clear it of the value-trap history that makes offshore E&C the classic 7532.T trap. Neither is true today.

It is on the list as the pricing benchmark that decides whether #2 is a mispricing or a correct discount, which is only checkable once both are fetched locally.

Sweep — 29 August 2026

1. Where the world is

What is true

The world is absorbing a genuine increase in electricity use, not just an AI-market narrative. The IEA expects global electricity demand to grow 3.6% in 2026 and 3.8% in 2027, versus 3.0% in 2025; it also expects renewables to overtake coal generation in 2026 and says grid expansion and modernisation are critical to integrating that supply (IEA mid-year update). The local data agree that the physical inputs have moved: copper is up 46.95% over one year, while WTI is up 30.35% over one year but down 9.46% over three months (local macro data).

That investment boom sits beside a less comfortable macro picture. The IMF forecasts 3.0% global growth in 2026 and says disinflation has stalled, with technology momentum offsetting the drag from war (IMF July update). Markets show the same split: Nasdaq is up 23.06% over one year and the S&P 500 19.37%, while the Hang Seng is down 0.13%; US five- and ten-year yields are up 21.14% and 11.66% respectively over one year (local macro data).

What I take from it

Power demand is real, but the first-order trade is crowded enough that a good backlog is no longer sufficient. GE Vernova, Caterpillar and Hammond Power Solutions all reported exceptional demand, but their obviousness is the reason not to promote them here (GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Hammond Power Solutions). The useful candidates are businesses where reported orders or cash generation improved while the price lagged, and where the next check can distinguish conversion from backlog theatre. That produces AMSC and OSIS below.

The stalled-disinflation backdrop also argues for not making this a fourth consecutive list of AI infrastructure names. Novo Nordisk is the counterweight: a familiar, profitable consumer-health franchise where the market is pricing a material deterioration in realised price and competitive position. NVIDIA appears only as a re-look because the newly revised local valuation scan fired on it after results; it is not being rediscovered by the Sweep.

2. Leo's reading

pot/reading.md still has no entry under Entries, but the saved-text folder contains the unlisted 2026-04-14-Convexity-Ivan-Li.md. I read the full saved text despite its absence from the list. It is a method essay, not a stock thesis: allow the right tail to compound, do not mechanically rebalance winners away, and do not confuse a price fall with a broken business.

Since 14 April, its named examples have dispersed: NVDA +10.71%, VOO +10.79%, META −12.75%, NFLX −23.11%, AMZN +6.99% and TSLA −4.24% through 28 August (local price history). That four-month spread neither proves nor disproves a long-horizon convexity argument; NVDA has merely matched VOO over the period.

The argument still fits the written rules. Strategy §5.1 permits a sale only when a falsifier trips, the thesis plays out, or a hard position limit is breached; a mechanical stop-loss and routine rebalancing are absent (strategy). The essay cannot override the 50% pot-position cap, and its claim that losers can be left alone still depends on business-level falsifiers being reviewed. It should produce no watchlist ticker.

3. Candidates

AMSC — Nasdaq — American Superconductor

Why: Revenue rose 30% to a record $94.1m, orders exceeded $130m, twelve-month backlog exceeded $300m and operating cash flow nearly quadrupled to $16m, yet the share price was down 43.40% over one year by 26 August (company results, price source). This is a quieter grid, mining-power and resiliency route than the large turbine and transformer winners.

What would have to be true: Acquired and organic revenue must turn into durable per-share earnings: first-quarter non-GAAP net income fell to $7.6m from $11.6m even as revenue grew, and the company warns that backlog may not convert and that suppliers and government funding matter (company results).

OSIS — Nasdaq — OSI Systems

Why: Fiscal-2026 revenue rose 4% to $1.786bn, non-GAAP EPS rose 11% to $10.35, operating cash flow reached a record $276m and backlog a record $1.9bn, while the shares were down 10.18% over one year at 28 August (company results, price source). Security scanning, optoelectronics and healthcare make it a second-order infrastructure/security name rather than a single-theme defence bet.

What would have to be true: Security deliveries delayed by the Middle East conflict must convert rather than roll forward indefinitely, and the fourth-quarter 4% revenue decline must be timing rather than lost demand. Management's fiscal-2027 target of 5.0–8.1% revenue growth and 7.5–11.0% non-GAAP EPS growth must show up in GAAP cash earnings, not only adjusted guidance (company results).

NVO — NYSE ADR / Nasdaq Copenhagen home listing — Novo Nordisk

Why: Q2 adjusted sales rose 7% and adjusted operating profit 11% at constant exchange rates, and guidance was raised, yet the ADR trades at 11.86 times trailing earnings and has returned only 1.78% over five years (company announcement, price and valuation). It is a profitable healthcare franchise outside the portfolio's technology-heavy centre, with pessimism visible in the multiple.

What would have to be true: GLP-1 volume must offset lower realised prices and intensifying competition without sacrificing earnings quality. The raised full-year range still calls for adjusted sales and operating profit to be flat to down 6%, and Q2 adjustments exclude a DKK6.3bn pipeline-asset impairment and 340B provision effects (company announcement, half-year filing).

NVDA — Nasdaq — NVIDIA — re-look (held)

Why: The revised local Scan now puts trailing P/E at 27.50, the lowest observation and 0th percentile across 261 weeks, while Q2 revenue rose 106% to $96.2bn, data-centre revenue rose 117% to $89.0bn and GAAP gross margin was 75.0% (local signal scan, company results).

What would have to be true: The earnings denominator must be durable: a five-year-low P/E is not the same as a cheap business if hyperscaler capital spending or 75% gross margins normalise. The market still values NVIDIA at $5.51tn and 18.36 times trailing sales, so the P/E signal needs a fresh cash-flow and customer-concentration check before it means value (market data).

4. What I wanted and did not have

  • Global electricity-demand, grid-investment and connection-queue data: fetched from the IEA. I would carry each new or mid-year report into the weekly Sweep, not poll it weekly; it separated genuine physical demand from company promotion.
  • Off-universe price and valuation history: fetched from Yahoo Finance, MarketBeat and Fox Business. This gap was already recorded in the wishlist earlier today; adding AMSC, OSIS and NVO to watchlist.json lets the existing pipeline replace the manual figures on its next run.
  • Company order/backlog conversion: fetched from AMSC and OSI releases. I would want it on results dates, not weekly; the local pipeline carries earnings and prices but not order quality.
  • GLP-1 realised pricing, volumes and material pipeline impairments: fetched from Novo Nordisk's announcement and SEC filing. Quarterly is sufficient; trailing P/E alone cannot distinguish a temporarily cheap franchise from declining economics.

The new gaps above were appended to pot/data-wishlist.md; the existing off-universe-price entry was not duplicated.

5. Sources consulted

Local: strategy.md, pot-design.md, pot/reading.md, the unlisted saved convexity article, holdings.json, watchlist.json, prices.json, history.json, signals.json, pot/positions.json, pot/data-wishlist.md, and both prior Sweep files.

External primary sources: IEA Electricity 2026 and its mid-year update; IMF July World Economic Outlook update; NVIDIA, GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Hammond Power Solutions, AMSC, OSI Systems, Amentum, Atkore and Novo Nordisk releases or filings. Secondary price and valuation checks: Yahoo Finance, StockAnalysis, MarketBeat and Fox Business. GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Hammond, Amentum and Atkore were screening work, not candidates; no commentary source was used as a company fact where a primary release was available.

7532.T check

docs.title: Paper performance
docs.html:
Paper performance

Generated 2026-09-12 00:38 by npm run pot-report, from history.json closes.

Every name this pot has named, marked from the day it was named, as if bought at that day's close and held. Nothing has been bought — pot cash is £0 and no contribution has been made, so this is not P&L. It exists because positions.js scores nothing until money is committed, which leaves the phase where you are deciding whether to commit with no measure at all.

Every row below is noise. Not one of the 92 marks has reached 20 trading days — the oldest is 10. Read this page for whether the plumbing works, not for whether the picks are any good.

Returns are in each name's local currency. FX is excluded on purpose: the question here is whether the name was a good call, not what a sterling investor would have banked. That second question matters — 7532.T sits in strategy.md as a yen-depreciation regret — and earns its own column when real money makes it a real return.

Deep dive proposals

Each proposal is marked separately, including re-proposals of a name already proposed: a name that keeps clearing the bar at a different price is making a different call each time, and averaging them would hide exactly that. ×N means the same name cleared the bar N times on one day — the cycle runs several times daily and those share a single closing price, so they are one mark and N calls, not N marks.

Cost

Cash cost: £0. Codex is authenticated against a ChatGPT subscription (codex login status → "Logged in using ChatGPT"), so nothing is billed per token. What a run spends is subscription allowance and wall-clock time.

The token columns are kept because that is D12's whole purpose: if this ever moves to metered API credits these are the numbers that would be charged, and runs either side of the switch stay comparable. Fresh is input not served from cache — the part a metered call charges full rate for.
